## [8.0.2665] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A request for a habitable world now gets a temperate world with air and a sea in nearly every system (a temperate sea world was present in 5 of 30 G2V systems before and 30 of 30 now), and the class of a world with life always matches the air it ends up with.

### Changed
- **A habitable request asks for conditions, not a class letter (GEN.916).** `generation/habitable_request.py`: a planet or moon meets the request when its solved surface is 273 to 323 K, its air at least 10 kPa and its water a surface ocean. The system retry, the forced and natural habitable slots, `build_planet` and the redraw that bars habitable worlds (`HABITABLE_WORLD` False) use it. The classes that "can carry life" included a hot reducing world, a glaciated one and a carbon dioxide one, so the letter was no test. The request is judged again on the finished bodies after the life pass (life changes the air and so the climate), and an unmet request says so in `unmet_requirements`.
- **The orbit of a habitable request is aimed by the climate the draw solved (GEN.911).** After two misses, each next draw goes to where the star's light would give 298 K (the distance goes as the square of the ratio of temperatures), kept inside the zone; the solve decides what each draw is. With the request on, 30 systems each: a temperate sea world is present in G2V 5 to 30 and K5V 2 to 28; the PHI-6 answer (aim/fallback/unmet) moved G2V 0/8/22 to 0/10/20 and K5V 0/5/25 to 2/13/15, because air and radiation, not climate, limit it now. Registry rows CC11 and CC12.
- **A stored class always matches the air it ends with (GEN.980).** The gas ledger of epoch 122 changes the air of hydrogen-eating (Class 3) worlds after their class was derived, so 25 of 2,835 bodies in a 120-system scan kept the class of the air before life. The class is now derived again after life changes the air.
- **Planet porosity (TEST.461).** `planets.porosity` is never written because a planet starts at the mass a body stops being a heap of grains; the round-trip test now says so and names GEN.780, which fills surface and crust porosity. No schema change.

## [8.0.2664] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** Acid-world, ammonia-water and silicon-in-acid life can now arise on worlds whose conditions fit, and sulfur, acid and cold-hydrogen life now change the air.

### Changed

- GEN.894: Classes 5, 8 and 9 now read real quantities instead of waiting for them. A world holds the acid medium of Classes 5 and 9 when its air makes a sulfuric acid cloud layer or pool (GEN.888); Class 8 reads the ammonia of its water, worked out from its ice and water shares; Class 9 also needs a silicon-rich crust (rock Mg/Si at or under 1). The acid classes get a reduced-sulfur supply from the air's sulfur dioxide, and the pool class (5b) and Class 9 need a pool, not just a cloud layer.

These are stand-in numbers, each with a tier and tweak level in the registry (LF61 and LF62).

## [8.0.2663] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A rocky planet's own water now follows the same delivery law as its air: more water the farther from the star and the heavier it is.

### Changed
- **GEN.849: a rocky body's bulk water is drawn from the Bern delivery model (`physics/delivered_water`).** The body takes a water class (dry, low, high or rich) from the law the atmosphere recipes b1 to b4 already read, by its mass and the snow lines it formed at, then a log-uniform share inside the class (the rich class runs from 10 percent to a cap of 50 percent of its mass). It replaces the old 97 percent dry range and 3 percent of ocean-world draw, which did not look at the planet's mass or how near the snow line it formed. A rocky planet formed close to the star is now mostly dry and more of those formed near the snow line hold an ocean's worth or more. Bodies beyond the snow line keep their ice-and-rock range. `tuning.DRY_WATER_MASS_FRACTION` and `WATER_WORLD_*` are gone; the registry rows are CC3 (the icy range) and DW1 to DW3.

## [8.0.2662] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** Every temperature on a world's page now shows the day and night range of its own place.

### Changed
- **GEN.848: a day and night swing is stored for every place that has a temperature.** Until now only the equator had one, so the polar, northern, southern and mean temperatures read "no day and night range stored for this place". Seven new columns on planets and moons (`temp_polar_swing_k`, `temp_north_swing_k`, `temp_south_swing_k`, `temp_mean_swing_k`, `temp_day_side_swing_k`, `temp_terminator_swing_k`, `temp_night_side_swing_k`; migration, schema v182) hold them. A band's swing is the equator's cut by the cosine of its latitude (the daily variation of the sunlight, which the ground and air carry linearly), the mean swing is the area-weighted mean of the bands, and a tidally locked world, which turns once an orbit and has no day, stores 0 for its three zones and says so on its page. The regions object of the API gains the same swings by name (`polar_swing`, `mean_swing`, ...). The climate sentence already states the equator's low and high and agrees with the page; it is unchanged.
- **Migration 0182 adds the columns empty;** a galaxy made earlier gets them when it is regenerated.

## [8.0.2659] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** Rocky planets are born spinning more slowly, so a free planet's day is now typically 7 hours instead of 3 and a Mars-sized planet can turn in a day.

### Changed
- **Birth spin retune, the interim of GEN.953.** The width of the Gaussian components of a rocky planet's birth spin (Kokubo and Genda 2010) is scaled by 0.4, and a planet under 0.3 Earth masses is slowed further in proportion to its mass. The median free day of a planet of 0.1 to 5 Earth masses goes from 2.9 hours to about 7 hours (Vesta 5.3 h, Ceres 9.1 h, the Earth after the Moon-forming impact about 5 h), more planets are tide-locked and the day and night swing, daylight and work-day readers move with the day. The random stream does not move (three Gaussian draws as before); values do. Registry rows SP11 and SP12 (tweak level L3) name Kokubo and Genda equation 4 with the last-impact mass-ratio law (GEN.978) as their replacement in GEN.979.

## [8.0.2647] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A giant's dynamo region and field can now be worked out from its interior layers (built, not wired in yet; nothing generated changes).

### Changed
- **The dynamo region of a giant (GEN.809, the lock-free half).** `physics/giant_dynamo.py` takes a giant's interior layers, its radius, the heat it radiates and its spin, finds the shell that carries its dynamo (the metallic hydrogen layer of a gas giant or brown dwarf, the conducting water of an ice giant's mantle; the helium gradient, helium shell and dilute core under a gas giant's are stable and left out) and gives the field of `dynamo.py` for it. Jupiter-like draws land within a factor of four of Jupiter's moment and differ with the drawn metallization pressure; a Saturn-like giant comes out weaker than a Jupiter-like one (still several times Saturn's own, the stable layer above its dynamo is not modelled); a slowly turning hot giant is multipolar; a Neptune-like ice giant lands within a factor of ten of Neptune's moment but as a dipole, which Neptune's field is not. The generator does not call it yet: the wiring step replaces the three giant anchors of `magnetism` and rides a train after the giant structure of GEN.733.

## [8.0.2639] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** `planetgen query near` rejects a missing distance before it opens the database, a document written to standard output starts at its first line, and ten tests that were red on main are green.

### Fixed

- **`planetgen query near` with neither `--distance` nor `--nearest` is a command-line error (TEST.465).** It exits 2 with the usage text whatever the state of the database; before, it opened the database first and exited 1 when it could not.
- **`planetgen system --output -` starts at the first line of the document (TEST.466).** The finished progress display wrote a blank line to standard output ahead of the text; a run that writes the document to standard output draws no bar.
- **Two saves of the same names at once no longer fail with "Transaction characteristics can't be changed while a transaction is in progress" (TEST.463).** The save ends the connection's open transaction before it sets READ COMMITTED.
- **The radiative-convective water table names its own limit (TEST.463).** The 640 K top of the table is `WATER_TABLE_TOP_K`, a numerical limit just under the critical temperature that `physics/saturation.py` holds; no vapour-pressure constant lives outside the saturation module. The cosmic-ray thin-air curve reads `GCR_PEAK_G_CM2` where it joins the first shower run (the same 100 g/cm2), so the registry row CR4 has a reader.
- **Tests that were red on main (TEST.463).** The step-kind registry test no longer reads a queue command's name as a progress step kind; the SQL portability list names the interest-count migrations that already use `VALUES()`; the object-row round trip reads a binary pair's stars, not the proxy that stands for both; `/api/auth/me` has an avatar field; the map-rebuild test stubs the sliced warm stages; the sector page test expects a second neighbourhood job to wait in the one waiting list (PERF.154); the wiring register no longer names `surface_dose`, which the code reads now.

## [8.0.2638] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** Drawing the nebula field can now follow another stage in the same run, the part of one run per Generate job that needs no other change.

### Changed

- PERF.203 step 2: the nebula field stage says "the galaxy's skeleton has never been built" and skips a galaxy with no outline when the stage opens (its `prepare` and `expand`), not when the command starts, so an earlier stage of the same run may be what builds the plan. `planetgen scatter --nebula-field` refuses and draws exactly what it did. The other fills (map luminosity, habitability, population, territories) had no start-time check to move. The scatters, link, settle and the sectors planner read the database to build their stages and are PERF.212 to PERF.214.

## [8.0.2637] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The All systems list opens any page as fast as the first when sorted by sector, octant or binary, as it already did by name.

### Changed
- **The All systems table pages by key in every sort.** Sorted by sector, octant or binary, the page links carry the system the page before ended on and the list carries on from it inside its group, so a page deep in the list costs what the first does. Before, a page counted and skipped every system before it in its group: with 3,000,000 systems, a page 300,000 deep in an octant took 1.5 seconds and now takes 3 milliseconds. `GET /api/systems?after=<system ID>` now works in those sorts as well as by name.

## [8.0.2636] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A world that suits a life class but where no life has started yet is no longer shown as having that life.

### Changed

- **No life class before life (GEN.1001).** A planet or moon round a star younger than the first step of its life schedule is stored with the life class it suits and no life stage, and it used to look as if that life lived there. The Galaxy Map life class marks, the life class filter and its count, the class shown in the search results and the habitability icons, the API's `life_class_id`, the dominant species line on the object page and the side panel of the system map now treat such a world as having no living class; the description of the world still says the conditions suit the class and none has appeared yet. A database made before this keeps the old map marks of those worlds until their systems are saved again.

## [8.0.2635] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The runs of the generation commands are now built apart from starting them, the first step toward one run for a whole Generate job.

### Changed

- PERF.203 step 1: each single-stage generation command (skeleton, bright-star and phenomena scatters, map luminosity, habitability, nebula field, clear scatter, link, backfill, settle, population, territories) builds its run as a `followed.Planned` (its followers, title and what it returns) and starts it with `followed.run_planned`. Nothing about what a command does or generates changes; the later steps put the planned runs of every selected command into one run.

## [8.0.2634] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The test suite now holds standing checks on the life classes: no star letter table, no stage without a class, no Flora under ice, and no class on a solvent it does not allow.

### Changed

- **Standing life class tests (GEN.873).** A new test file checks the life class rules against the shared body sweep and the generated systems: the class rules hold no table keyed by a star letter and every star letter feeds some light class, a body with a life stage has a life class, no light class is supported and no body has Flora under an ice-covered ocean, and no class is supported or lives where its solvent (water, hydrocarbon, liquid carbon dioxide, sulfuric acid or ammonia water) is missing. Each rule is shown to fail on a body made to break it. Nothing the generator draws changes.

## [8.0.2633] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** "Near this system" now measures from where the system really is, and four more tests that were red on main are green.

### Fixed

- **A system's page and the near command put the system in the wrong place (TEST.453).** The galaxy position an object page and `near` read for a system added the system's offset to its sector centre without turning it by the sector's orientation, so it sat up to a couple of parsecs from the point stored with it (the position every map and search uses). `near` and `nearest` from a system now measure from the stored point, and the system's own sector-local position on its page is unchanged.
- **A moon whose tide works out to nothing stored 0 and not none (TEST.453).** An icy moon on a circular orbit saved a tidal flux of exactly 0.0 while a rocky one saved none; both are none now, so a saved moon's tide is empty or positive.
- **A world around a black hole could stop a system from generating (TEST.453).** A black hole's temperature gives no visible light, and the atmosphere colour of a giant lit by it raised "the spectrum has no light between 380 and 780 nm"; a body lit by a star with no visible light now has no atmosphere colour, as one with no star temperature already did.
- **Two planet page tests expected a class name the page no longer has (TEST.453).** The summary paragraph is `summary inline-links` since UX.220; the tests now look for that.

## [8.0.2632] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** K dwarfs are 11% of stars instead of 19%, and an M dwarf has a companion star as often as the star-count table says.

### Fixed
- **K and M stars were split at the wrong temperature (GEN.897).** The K class ran down to 3700 K, so stars of 0.4 to 0.55 solar masses, M0 to M2 in the surveys, came out K8 and K9: K was 19.4% of stars against 11.6% (RECONS) to 12.9% (Mamajek) observed. The K/M edge is now 3900 K (M0V is 3850 K; the luminosity ranges already put it near there) and the A/F edge 7200 K (F0V is 7220 K): K is 10.8% and M 76.7% of the stars at the reference solar position, both inside the researched ranges, and A rises from 0.11% to 0.15%. The class page and the map colours read the same edges. Stand-in row SC1 (T2, L1).
- **An M dwarf lost its companions to brown dwarfs (GEN.899).** A companion's mass was drawn from 0.1 to 1 times its primary's, so more than half of the companions of a low-mass M dwarf were under 0.08 solar masses, were cut out of the system, and left an M2V primary with a companion star in 15.8% of systems against the star-count table's 27%. Every other star of a tree is now at least 0.08 solar masses, so the table counts stars (M2V: 26.6%), and a brown dwarf is one extra member in 3% of the drawn trees (`tuning.BROWN_DWARF_COMPANION_CHANCE`, stand-in row SC2, T2, L0; it was about 17% of M2V trees). A forced star count adds none, and a tree's `star_count` no longer counts one.
- **A stars stay rare (GEN.898, closed with the residual documented).** The disk history behind the age mix matches the observed present star formation rate over its mean and the B star share, so the shortfall of A stars (0.15% against 0.6% to 1.1%, which rests on 4 stars of 378) is left as a documented known anomaly in the star census instead of a tuned mix. The census also keeps G dwarfs (3.1% against 4.1% to 5.0%) as a known anomaly: the mass function gives too few stars of 0.86 to 1.1 solar masses.
- **Day and night shares followed the spin before an orbit move (GEN.904).** After a planet's orbit was moved to clear a neighbour, its spin was drawn again but its solar day and hours of daylight were left as they were (or, for a reclassified planet, were left empty: 158 of 1,100 rotating planets in the sample): a planet with a 2.02 hour rotation showed a 3.41 hour solar day. The shares are worked out again from the new spin and orbit, for the planet and each of its moons.
- **Class V and other worlds that keep their hydrogen had no mantle oxidation (GEN.905).** An envelope's air mixture carries no mantle redox, so `mantle_redox` and `mantle_delta_iw` were empty on class V; they come from the same redox rows as an airless rocky body's now, and the sheet fill audit no longer excuses them.

## [8.0.2631] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The phenomena census now measures a galaxy that is Milky Way-like, so the supernova remnant, magnetar and Wolf-Rayet counts it reported as too low were the test galaxy's, not the generator's.

### Changed

- **The phenomena census reads a Milky Way-like galaxy (GEN.900, GEN.901, GEN.902).** The old reference galaxy had a bulge as heavy as its thin disk and no mass chain, so its star formation history ran on a galaxy a half larger than the stars its density held: it held 0.46 of the young and massive stars that history implied, and the supernova remnants (260), magnetars (22) and Wolf-Rayet stars (590) all fell short of their surveys. The census now draws its galaxy through the generator's own shape chain (5.2 billion solar masses of stars, a fifth of them in the bulge, a 2.6 kpc disk), where the density, the history and the mass agree and star formation is 1.9 solar masses a year (the Milky Way's 1.65). It finds 411 supernova remnants, 42 magnetars and 985 Wolf-Rayet stars, all inside their ranges, and the three known-anomaly tags are removed. Tests and test data only: no generated galaxy, system or planet changes.

## [8.0.2630] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The ground a planet is drawn with and its cloud, haze and dust draws no longer depend on its class letter.

### Changed
- **The dominant surface material and the aerosol draws follow the conditions, not the class (GEN.917, GEN.915).** The surface draw took the class letter in its inputs (for the giant check and as the key of its table, all of whose rows are open to every class); it now takes whether the body is a giant, from its structure, and draws the dominant ground from the composition, temperature, pressure and age alone, as its conditions already did. The aerosol stream was seeded with the class letter among its identity; it is now seeded from the body's identity (moon or planet, mass, radius, distance) and its conditions (surface temperature, air pressure). Bodies that carried a class letter at that point of generation draw different cloud, haze and dust depths.

generation-output: changed

## [8.0.2629] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A world whose only liquid is a puddle of concentrated chloride brine now reads "Brine seep" instead of "Surface ocean", and it no longer counts as a sunlit sea for life.

### Changed
- **Brine seep (GEN.908).** A liquid surface with so little water (under 2e-5 of the body's mass) that its chemistry is a concentrated chloride brine, melting at 200 to 270 K and often under no air, is its own water state, `brine seep`, on the page, the map and in the search. It still holds liquid water for a base and its ocean details are shown, but it is not a sunlit sea for life, not a wet world for plate tectonics and not an induction ocean. About two thirds of the worlds that used to read "Surface ocean" in a sun's habitable zone were such seeps.
- **Database.** Migration 0176 lets `planets` and `moons` store the new state and relabels the stored brine oceans.

generation-output: changed

## [8.0.2628] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A giant's temperature at its 1 bar level now includes its own heat, so a Jupiter-like giant at 5 AU is near 155 K instead of 135 K and Neptune-like ones near 75 K.

### Changed
- **Giant 1 bar temperature (GEN.816).** The stored temperature of a gas or ice giant radiates the starlight it absorbs and its own heat together. The own heat is the cooling law through Jupiter and Neptune (a Jupiter-like giant 5.6 W/m2 at 4.5 Gy, fading with age, rising with mass), replacing the old square-root-of-mass stand-in; the same flux feeds the temperature that decides helium rain and the temperature the giant's gas mixture is drawn at. Jupiter-, Uranus- and Neptune-like giants land at 154, 83 and 76 K against 166, 76 and 72 K measured; a Saturn-like one at 115 K against 134 K until its helium-rain heat is added (GEN.810). The temperature, pressure-level mixture and helium-rain verdict of every giant change.

generation-output: changed

## [8.0.2627] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** Radiation doses on thin-air worlds and the ozone layer now follow measured physics.

### Changed
- **The cosmic-ray dose of a thin or absent air column (GEN.746).** Between no air (the Moon) and 100 g/cm2 of air the dose is no longer a straight line between anchors: it is the cosmic-ray primaries thinned by nuclear collisions plus a shower that builds up with depth, fitted to the Moon, to Mars (232 mSv/yr at 22.6 g/cm2 and the slope Guo measured) and to the shower peak of the Atri table. A world with 0.1 to 50 g/cm2 of air now has a dose that rises toward the peak the way real columns do.
- **The dose from a star's particle storms (GEN.747).** The old 20 mSv/yr constant is replaced by the sum of 47 measured solar particle events (1997 to 2015), taken at the blood-forming organs: about 265 mSv/yr in free space at the Sun's distance, less what an air column and a magnetic field keep out. Other stars scale by their flare rate and distance. Worlds with thin air and no field now score worse on radiation; the ozone-loss flag follows the new numbers.
- **The ozone layer's temperature and spread (GEN.748).** The visible (Chappuis) absorption of ozone now depends on temperature, read from the Burkholder and Talukdar tables (cached on the next setup download of the ozone data), at the temperature of each body's ozone layer rather than a fixed 220 K. The spread of the ozone column around its median is now the range the published models give at each oxygen level, narrower where they agree, instead of one wide range everywhere.
- The stand-ins of all three are in the registry (gap-filling plan 6.23, rows CR1 to CR4, SE1 to SE5, OZ1 to OZ3), each with its source tier and tweak level.
- generation-output: changed

## [8.0.2626] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The stars of a globular cluster, a young cluster or a satellite galaxy now draw their composition from their own component instead of a halo value.

### Changed

- **Cluster and satellite stars take their component's [Fe/H] (GEN.662).** The stars the component pass places in a cluster or a satellite draw their birth [Fe/H] from that component's own value (with the scatter of its family) before their lifetimes and giant branch are worked out, and the row stores it. A star with no component given takes the generic cluster or satellite distribution; the halo's value, and the reference 0 their trees were read at, are gone from those paths.
- **A population's star counts are worked out at its own composition (GEN.661).** The number of stars in a mass band or above a luminosity used to be read at the Sun's composition for every population. A metal-poor population (a halo, a cluster) now has the larger bright share its stars have, and a metal-rich one the smaller. The stand-in left is the composition of the counts: one value, the population's mean at the Sun's distance (registry row SCC1).

## [8.0.2625] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The colour of a world's sky now takes the colour of its own ground, ice and bare rock, and a moon keeps how it formed.

### Changed
- **The ground under the air is the body's stored surface mix (GEN.462).** The atmosphere colour of a rocky planet or moon is worked out over the area-weighted reflectance of its stored ground types and ice in the three visible bands (the laboratory spectra of the materials table, held flat beyond 450 to 650 nm). The share of the surface with no measured visible spectrum (the open ocean and the metal) keeps the old stand-in reflectance of 0.15, and so does the whole ground of a body with no stored mix. The sky of a thick air above bright ice or salt is slightly lighter than above dark carbon or basalt. The weathering of an airless surface and the Bond albedo of the temperature stay with GEN.684.
- **A moon's origin and its giant's disk are stored (DB.70).** `moons` and `planets` gain `moon_origin` (disk, impact, captured, ring or binary) and, on a giant, the lifetime, alpha over f, ice fraction and ice-line distance of the disk its moons formed in (schema 169). A moon made before keeps empty columns.

## [8.0.2624] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** Massive stars born in the youngest star-forming regions can now come with a small group of siblings a fraction of a light year away.

### Changed
- **Young groups at fill (GEN.328).** An O or early-B star younger than 0.3 million years that the fill makes in an emission region (class D or E) is born in a group of three to five stars in 5% of cases (the Orion Trapezium is the model). Its group mates are separate young systems a few thousand to thirty thousand AU from it, built by whichever sector holds each one, so a group across a sector border is made once. A group older than its decay age (10,000 to 40,000 years) is not drawn: the star is built with the tighter hierarchy the group left, one star fewer. The protostars of star-forming cores are all under 8 solar masses, so none of them is massive enough to be in a group. Because an emission region's stars are usually older than 0.3 million years, groups are rare in the fill.

generation-output: changed

## [8.0.2623] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The Phenomena list opens any page, sorted by name, as fast as the first, and every page of it is quicker to open.

### Changed
- **The Phenomena table pages by key when sorted by name** (its default). The page links carry the phenomenon the page before ended on, so a page deep in the list costs what the first does: the list walks each phenomenon table's name index and the best of those is merged in the database, where it sorted every table whole for each page. With 8,000,000 built phenomena the first page by name went from about 45 seconds to 10 milliseconds, and a page after a built row takes 4 to 6 milliseconds. `GET /api/phenomena` takes `after=<type>:<ID>` of a built row for it.
- **No page counts every phenomenon first.** A page that starts at the top, in any sort, no longer counts all the built phenomena to know where the scattered ones start; only a page that starts past some of them does. The other sorts (type, descriptor, radius, sector, on the Galaxy Map) still sort the whole list for a page.
- **Within equal names, a descending sort now lists the types and ids in reverse too.**
- **Two more name indexes** (asteroid fields and interstellar comets), built online by the update.

## [8.0.2622] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The docs now have a page on the bulk composition data model: what a planet or moon is made of and how its mass, radius, density and gravity follow.

### Changed

- **The bulk composition page (DOC.65).** A new reference page names every stored value of a body's bulk composition (the metal, rock, water, ice and envelope shares, the rock and envelope details, porosity, the giant interior summary, mass, radius, density and gravity) with its unit, and describes the order of the work, the draw from the host star's abundances, the structure model that gives the radius, the giant radius law, the materials table, the composition words, the migration and the consistency sweep, with the sources of every number.

## [8.0.2621] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** Bringing a galaxy to the running generator epoch now draws a scatter that is behind again, instead of stopping and telling you to do it by hand.

### Changed

- **A stale scatter is redrawn by the bring-to-epoch run (GEN.845).** When an epoch has changed a scatter (the massive stars, the bright stars, the phenomena or the nebula field), `planetgen bring-to-epoch` and the Generate page's task no longer refuse. The run empties the sectors it will generate again (a scatter leaves a filled sector out), clears the stale scatters and draws them with the settings they were drawn with (luminosity floor, stellar mass limit, compact object limit), the massive stars before the bright stars that are split from them, then generates the emptied sectors again. A sector left alone because of an admin edit keeps the objects it was made with. If a scatter fails the emptied sectors stay empty and the run says how to finish by hand. Nothing a generator draws changes, so there is no epoch.

## [8.0.2620] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The Species list opens any page as fast as the first one, whatever the number of species, when sorted by name, era, tech level or spacefaring.

### Changed
- **The Species table pages by key.** The page links carry the species the page before ended on, so a page deep in the list costs what the first does; before, each page read and threw away every species before it. At a million species a deep page by name went from 8 seconds to 4 milliseconds, and the first page by era or tech level from 5 to 13 seconds to 4 milliseconds. `GET /api/species` takes `after=<species id>` for the same.
- **Sorted by name, era, tech level or spacefaring, the list reads in index order** (new indexes, built online by the update). Sorted by homeworld or system it still sorts every species, since those names live in other tables (the polity sort is quick too, as few species have a polity).
- **Within equal values, a descending sort now lists the names in reverse too** (it kept the names in order before).

## [8.0.2619] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The docs now have a page on the atmosphere data model: what a planet or moon stores about its air and where each value comes from.

## [8.0.2614] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A sweep test now checks that an Earth-like world's air settles from a cooling to a warming change of sunlight and measures its response against the published climate sensitivity.

### Added
- **Climate sensitivity sweep test (GEN.975).** The surface-air fixed point of an Earth-twin, with Earth's ocean, is solved at 90 to 110 percent of its absorbed sunlight. Every solve must converge, the surface must warm with the light, and the response must not exceed the upper end of the published range (AR6, 2 to 5 K per doubling, 0.54 to 1.35 K per W/m2). The lower end is held by a strict expected failure that names the three missing feedbacks (GEN.972 ice-albedo, GEN.973 water vapour, GEN.974 cloud albedo): the response is about 0.4 K per W/m2 today, and the mark has to come off when the feedbacks land.

## [8.0.2609] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** Zooming into a sector at the galaxy's core no longer gets stuck when the wheel points at a neighbouring empty cell.

### Changed
- **The wheel opens the sector again (TEST.450).** At the core the cells are small and close, so the wheel could land on a neighbouring cell nothing was generated in. The map asked the server for that cell's scene on every tick (a 404 each time), and each ask took the place of the real sector's scene load, which was then given up for good: the sector never opened and the zoom stopped about 1.4 parsecs out. An empty cell is now asked once, and a scene load that was only pushed aside is asked again.

**Headline:** The API names the life class of a planet or moon and the score of every class it supports.

The API version is now 10.

## [8.0.2607] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The mass boundary table no longer shows a TODO item code in the text it prints.

## [8.0.2605] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** What ices a comet holds (carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide) can now be worked out from where in its star's disc it formed (not yet used by the generator).

### Changed

- New library `physics/comet_ice_budget.py`: the disc's snow lines for water, carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide round a star of any luminosity, the CO2/H2O and CO/H2O of a body formed in each zone (from the disc's carbon and oxygen), and the share of a disc's comets in each zone. A carbon-monoxide-rich interstellar comet like 2I/Borisov comes out as a body from beyond its star's CO line. Nothing in generation reads it yet; the wiring step (the comet sampler taking its medians from the zone) follows with the epoch train.

## [8.0.2604] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The generator can now tell where a world holds liquid sulfuric acid, the medium of acid-world life.

### Changed

- GEN.888: a new reader works out from a world's air whether it has a sulfuric acid cloud layer (like Venus's temperate clouds) or an acid pool on warm dry ground, and how strong the acid is. It needs sulfur dioxide, an oxidiser and a trace of water, keeps to the 283 to 373 K liquid window and 0.3 to 3 bar for clouds, and counts acid of 81 percent by weight or stronger. Nothing is stored and nothing changes on a generated world yet; the life class rules read it when the wiring lands with the next generation epoch.
- The air-profile helper accepts the temperature the air turns isothermal at, so a hot thick air gets a cold top from the absorbed starlight instead of a fixed fraction of its surface temperature.

## [8.0.2603] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A rock's kind (basalt, granite, anorthosite and so on) can now be worked out from the oxides of the rock and how much of it melted, instead of copied from the Earth's crust (not yet used by the generator).

### Changed

- New library `physics/rock_types.py`: the CIPW norm of a set of oxides, the melt of a rock by stages with the enrichment of K, Th and U, and the ground type of the result by the standard silica bands. Nothing in generation reads it yet; the wiring step (the surface draw taking its crust from the stored mantle) follows with the epoch train.

## [8.0.2602] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The meteorite groups (CI, CM, ordinary, enstatite and the rest) can now be told apart from a body's own composition instead of being fixed inputs (not yet used by the generator).

### Changed

Nothing in generation reads it yet; the wiring step (labelling belts and replacing the fixed within-family splits of the taxon kernel) follows with the epoch train.

## [8.0.2601] - 2026-10-30

## [8.0.2579] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The light of a star can now be looked up from model-atmosphere spectra by temperature and gravity, with the corona's far ultraviolet added from the MUSCLES stars.

PHOENIX-ACES M-dwarf spectra (130 MB, reduced to a 2.5 MB table of power shares). `physics/stellar_library.py` gives the share of a star's power in each band from its effective temperature and gravity, and adds the chromosphere's far ultraviolet from its XUV power. It reproduces the Sun's measured ultraviolet shares to 15 percent and the near-ultraviolet of the eleven MUSCLES stars to 0.33 dex. ## [8.0.2578] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A neutron star's radius and layers can now be computed from the 21 equation-of-state tables by integrating the general-relativity structure equations.

### Added
- **Neutron star structure from an equation of state (GEN.968).** `physics/neutron_star_structure.py` integrates the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations over the 21 Malik, Pais and Providencia 2024 tables: a star's mass, radius, compactness, crust and neutron-drip radii, each table's mass-radius curve and maximum mass (2.0 to 2.75 solar masses), and the radius band the tables span at a mass (R of 1.4 solar masses: 11.8 to 13.8 km against NICER's 12.45 +- 0.65). Nothing in generation calls it yet; the wiring is GEN.969. Three stand-ins registered (NS1 to NS3).

## [8.0.2577] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A birth-spin module gives a rocky planet's spin from the mass ratio of its last impacts, so a Mars-sized planet can turn in a day while an Earth turns in hours.

### Added
- **`physics/impact_spin.py` (GEN.978).** Kokubo and Genda 2010 equation 4 (the spin a planet's last impacts leave, in breakup spins, from their mass ratio) and a registered stand-in for the distribution of that ratio by planet mass: planets of an embryo's mass often have had no giant impact and spin slowly, larger planets are built by giant impacts and spin faster. A draw over 0.1 to 5 Earth masses has a median day of 7 hours against the built spin's 2.9, half of Mars-mass planets turn in 24 hours or slower, and the range runs from 1.3 hours to some thousand hours (the widest of Kokubo and Genda and Miguel and Brunini). Nothing calls it yet; GEN.979 wires it into the planet's birth spin.
- **Stand-in rows GS1 to GS7** in the gap-filling plan (section 6.26) and the stand-in list.

Nothing in generation reads them yet, so generated output does not change; `./update.sh` fetches them.

## [8.0.2575] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A moon orbit module follows a planet's moons drifting out, spiralling in or falling into a ring under the planet's tide, ready for the tide chain to use.

### Added
- **`physics/moon_orbits.py` (GEN.958, stage 3a of the tide chain).** A pure module that integrates a planet's spin and all its moons' orbits together under the tide each moon raises: a moon of a fast-spinning planet drifts outward (the Moon at 3.7 cm a year), a moon of a slow or tide-locked planet or a retrograde moon (Phobos, Triton) spirals in, and one that reaches the Roche limit becomes ring material and gives its angular momentum to the planet. It also returns the heat the moons' tides put into the planet. Angular momentum is conserved. Nothing calls it yet; GEN.959 wires it into the moons, the rings and the planet's heat.
- **`spin_torques.Torques.softness`:** an optional smoothing of the constant-Q torque's sign flip, used by the integration.
- **Stand-in rows TM1 to TM4** in the gap-filling plan (section 6.25) and the stand-in list.

## [8.0.2574] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A new test keeps the generator from making a giant whose radius is read at the wrong light.

### Changed
- **Guard for giants that are bright and eccentric (GEN.977).** A giant's radius is read from the tables at the light of its orbit's semi-major axis, because the eccentricity is drawn after the radius. That is within 1% of the radius at the orbit's mean light unless the giant gets more than 300 times Earth's light and an eccentricity over 0.3 together. A seeded sweep now fails if the generator ever makes one, and the bound is written into the stand-in registry (OE12). Nothing you see on a planet changes.

## [8.0.2573] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A dynamo module gives a planet's magnetic moment from the power that drives its core and its spin, tested on Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Ganymede, Mercury and a dead Mars; nothing uses it yet.

### Added

- **The field of a dynamo from its power and spin (GEN.966).** The new `planetgen/physics/dynamo.py` takes the power that drives a core (or a giant's metallic layer), the region's radii and density and the spin, and gives the dipole moment, the local Rossby number, the dipole's share and the field at the core-mantle boundary or the surface. The strength is the buoyancy-flux scaling of Olson and Christensen (2006), `B = 0.2 sqrt(rho mu0 / 2) (F D)^(1/3)`; the Rossby number from the same power gates the dipole as it did before (`f_dip` falls through 0.12), so a slowly turning body has a weaker, multipolar field. A dynamo's lifetime is read from the history of its power (`lifetime`), and a giant is driven by a tenth of the heat it radiates. Earth gives 7.8e22 A m2 from 1.15 TW, Jupiter 1.6e27 against 1.5e27 observed, Ganymede 1.0e20 against 1.3e20; Saturn comes out six times too strong and Mercury twenty-two times (a stable layer weakens both, which the scaling does not model: the module takes an attenuation for it). A dead Mars has no power and no field. `magnetism.dipole_share` now calls the module's rule, with the same results. Four stand-in rows (DY1 to DY4, section 6.30 of the gap plan) record the numbers that are not measured. Nothing stored changes: GEN.967 replaces the design defaults with it.

## [8.0.2572] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A spin torque module sums a planet's star, moon and thermal-tide torques and runs its spin to the state they leave it in, ready for the tide chain to use.

### Added
- **`physics/spin_torques.py` (GEN.956, stage 2a of the tide chain).** A pure module for the torques on a planet's spin: the star's tide, each moon's tide (a moon inside corotation spins the planet up, the Earth-Moon day lengthens 2 ms a century) and the thermal tide of a thick air (Leconte et al. 2015, tabulated for 1, 10 and 92 bar), with a spin evolution that stops at a resonance, a synchronous state, a moon's corotation or a balance of the thermal and gravitational tides (the asynchronous states of Venus-like planets). With one star and a constant Q it gives the same spins as the built despinning. Nothing calls it yet; GEN.957 wires it into planet spin.
- **Stand-in rows TQ1 to TQ6** in the gap-filling plan (section 6.24) and the stand-in list.

## [8.0.2571] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** A tidal rheology module gives a body's Love number and quality factor from its mantle's temperature, melt and the tide's frequency, ready for the tide chain to use.

### Added
- **`physics/tidal_rheology.py` (GEN.954, stage 1a of the tide chain).** A pure function of mass, radius, tide frequency, mantle temperature, melt share and the body's own drawn mantle viscosity (Andrade or Maxwell rheology, Henning et al. 2009, Efroimsky 2012) that returns `k2` and `Q`. It gives the Moon its measured Love number and a Q of 61, Io `k2/Q` of a few hundredths in partial melt with no number fitted to Io, and the solid Earth a semi-diurnal Q of a few hundred. Nothing calls it yet; GEN.955 wires it into the tidal heat, the interior heat and the circularisation time.
- **Stand-in rows TR1 to TR10** in the gap-filling plan (section 6.23) and the stand-in list, each with its source tier and tweak level, and a design note, `docs/design/orbits/tidal-chain.md`.
- **Census check of GEN.954** on 8,822 generated rocky planets and moons: with the rheology's Q instead of 100, 18.9 percent of free planets and 5.9 percent of free moons would lock, and 3 to 6 percent flip between tide-above-own-heat and below it (note at `docs/design/orbits/tidal-chain.md`).

## [8.0.2570] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The property sheet audit no longer excuses the moons' induced magnetic moment as an open gap; the column has been filled since the ocean-moon induction was built.

### Fixed

- **The induced moment of a moon is no longer listed as a known gap (GEN.779).** The fill audit excused the moons' `induced_moment_a_m2` as an open gap, written when the column was believed empty. A moon's induced dipole is set in the final pass of every system (`magnetism.generate_induced_field`, GEN.178: the moon's ocean answering its parent's turning field, 0 for a moon with no liquid ocean, no parent field or a parent that turns with it); a sample of 30 systems has it filled on every moon and non-zero for the ice-covered-ocean moons. The excuse is removed, so the audit now fails if the column is ever empty again. A planet keeps its sheet rule (it orbits its star alone, and its field answer is the part of GEN.779 that rides a train). No stored value or generated output changes.

## [8.0.2569] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The young-star planet test checks that no life is drawn, not which class letter a planet gets.

### Changed
- TEST.462: `test_planets_respect_their_stars_age_and_history` failed now and then because it required that no planet of a star under 0.1 Gy carry a class letter from `HABITABLE_PLANET_CLASSES`. Since the class cut-over (GEN.646) the letter is derived from the finished conditions and says nothing of life (GEN.915), so a class V world around a 0.08 Gy star is right as long as it holds no life. The test now asserts that these planets and their moons have no life class. The test draws unseeded systems, which is why the failure showed only in some runs and orders.

## [8.0.2568] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** Stepping from an open system on the Galaxy Map now crosses the sector's edge to the nearest system that way.

### Changed
- **System steps cross the sector's edge (MAP.329).** With a system opened in place, the step buttons and keys (north, south, east, west, out, in) used to reach only the systems of the same sector. They now also read the sectors round it, and go to the nearest system lying that way even when it is in the next sector: that sector opens beside the first, the system in it, and the scale is kept. The neighbours are not drawn.

## [8.0.2567] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The skeleton, clear-scatter and clean-nebula-field commands now run as stages of the shared run, so they can share one run with other commands.

### Changed
- **Three one-step commands start their run through the shared stage list (PERF.202).** `planetgen plan` (the skeleton), `planetgen clear-scatter` and `planetgen clean-nebula-field` each used to start a one-step run of their own; they now follow a stage of the shared run like the other commands, so two of them can run in one run and keep their refusals, in order. The output is unchanged; a stopped run of these now also records the galaxy seed and build so `planetgen finish-run` can carry it on.

## [8.0.2566] - 2026-10-30

**Headline:** The browser test that clicks a black hole, a neutron star and a quasar on the Galaxy Map finds each by its tooltip, so a wheel step that moves them a few pixels no longer sends its click elsewhere.

### Fixed

- **The point-phenomena link test no longer clicks blind (TEST.459).** `test_galaxy_map_draws_point_phenomena_that_link_to_their_pages` computed where the map draws each point and clicked there and at eight offsets around it, taking the first click that named the point. Since the wheel heads for the crowd of stars in front of the pointer (MAP.301) the steps in land the view a few pixels differently, the neutron star's spot fell under the fixture nebula's core, and the next offset clicked empty space beside it, which opens the sector block under the pointer and flies the camera there, so the quasar was selected and the test left the map. The test now moves the pointer over the same offsets and clicks only where the tooltip names the point. No map behaviour, stored value or generated output changes.

## [8.0.2565] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** A new Properties page in the Help menu explains where every value on a planet, moon or star page comes from.

### Changed
- **Properties help page (UX.187).** The Help menu has a Properties page that lists each value shown on a planet, moon or star page with its unit and the step of the generation that fixes it. A planet, moon or star page links to it from "Where these values come from".

## [8.0.2564] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** Worlds with life now hold the gases their kind of life makes at their stage: methane and hydrogen drawdown for the hydrogen, donor and anoxygenic classes, a methane haze that follows it, and no methane once the oxygen has risen.

### Changed
- **The class gas ledger (GEN.891, GEN.857, GEN.858, GEN.859).** `physics/data/life_ledger.json` holds one row per life class and `physics/life_air.py` applies it after the oxygen. A built class (1, 2, 3, 6 and 8) that has producers by the star's age puts methane into an air with no free oxygen: its flux (the carbon the oxygenic class buries, or the donor and hydrogen supplies of the other classes over Earth's) times the 30,000 year life of methane, at most 3.5 percent of the air's molecules, with the carbon taken from the air's own carbon dioxide (a tenth of the carbon stays). The hydrogen eaters draw hydrogen down to 1e-4 of the molecules. An oxygenic class makes no methane once its oxygen has risen. The haze, ultraviolet shield, colour and habitability score are redone from the air life leaves. Classes 4, 5, 7 and 9 are `pending` rows and change nothing yet. Every number has a tier and tweak level (row LF60). The haze's cooling of the ground and the hydrosphere of a world the new air moves across freezing are not modelled.
- **Icy-moon tide (GEN.906).** An icy body on an orbit so round that its tide underflows to 0.0 now stores no tide (NULL), as a rocky body does, instead of 0.0.
- **Magnetopause in planet radii (GEN.843).** `magnetopause_rp` was stored in Earth radii but labelled planet radii, so any body not Earth-sized read wrong by the ratio of radii. It now divides the standoff by the body's own radius.

generation-output: changed

TODO items resolved: GEN.891, GEN.857, GEN.858, GEN.859, GEN.906, GEN.843. Added: stand-in registry row LF60.

## [8.0.2563] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The physics rows on a star, planet or moon page now say where their value comes from.

### Changed
- **A one-line source under each physics value (UX.187).** The eccentricity and inclination of an orbit, the tidal and interior heat, the Urey ratio and the tectonic regime, thorium and uranium, the spin and tilt, the magnetic moment, the ring edge and optical depth, and the five life ages now carry one sentence under the number that says how it was worked out and which generator item does it (for example the Kepler multi-planet law for an eccentricity, or Peale, Cassen and Reynolds for tidal heat). The API sheet row has the same text as `source`. Only values that are stored on main are covered; a row whose rule is not written down has no line, and the rows of values still being added (the escape and delivery history, the star states) get theirs when their columns land. Nothing generated or stored changes.

## [8.0.2562] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** One "Go to" for every move on the Galaxy Map, a find-a-place box that takes names, coordinates, sector designations, object IDs, regions and recent places, and a log ruler with named, clickable scales.

### Changed
- **One verb, "Go to" (MAP.336).** Every animated move on the Galaxy Map is now called Go to: the buttons that said "Fly to" and "Zoom in on them", the sector wall icons and the double click all go through one function. Zoom is only the wheel, the plus and minus buttons, the slider, the pinch and the keys.
- **Find a place.** The address box is now a find-a-place box (press `/` anywhere on the page to reach it). As you type it lists what the line can be: coordinates (`x y z` in parsecs), a sector designation or shell/band/wedge, an object ID (its system opens, and a planet or moon is picked), charted regions by name, names the server finds, and places you went to before (an empty box lists them, and the way to the whole galaxy). Enter or a click goes there.
- **A log ruler.** The zoom slider became a vertical log ruler: the whole galaxy at the top, a moon at the bottom, a named stop for each scale (galaxy, arm and halo, region, sector, neighbourhood, planetary system, planet, moon), each a Go to for that scale about the middle of the map, and a readout of the distance and the nearest thing. A card on the right now stands to the left of the ruler.
- **Crumbs and Up.** Each crumb is a Go to for what it names, and the Up button is "Up one level".
- **Where Go to a region lands.** A region is framed on its charted part by default. A browser setting, `map.regionLanding` (`densest`), lands on the cluster of the region's heaviest sectors instead; the setting's own page is UX.236.

## [8.0.2561] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The masses where one kind of object gives way to another are one table, each with its source and how sure it is.

### Changed

- **One table of mass boundaries (GEN.933).** The edge of a brown dwarf and a star (0.08 solar masses), the planet and brown dwarf edge (13 Jupiter masses), the heaviest brown dwarf (80), the core collapse edge (8 solar masses), the white dwarf progenitor floor (0.8), Chandrasekhar's limit and the spectral class mass edges were typed in several modules each. They are now `physics/mass_boundaries.py`, with a source and a tier for every row, and the mass function, companions, rogue bodies, plausibility bounds and the disk history read them there. Nothing generated changes. The table records one disagreement it does not settle: 80 Jupiter masses is 0.0764 solar masses, so a stretch under the star floor of 0.08 is empty; GEN.936 closes it.

## [8.0.2560] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** A scattered star or phenomenon with a neutron star or black hole in a close pair now says what kind of pair it is.

### Changed
- **Compact binaries on the pages and in the API (UX.186).** The page of an uncharted star or phenomenon that holds an X-ray binary or a spider pulsar gains a Compact binaries panel: the kind (high-mass X-ray binary, Be/X-ray binary, low-mass X-ray binary, black widow or redback), the compact object, its companion, and whether the accretor is a microquasar. The same list is in the API as `compact_pairs`, and the stored `flags` of members and the `interaction` and `flags` of orbits are now returned too. The X-ray luminosity is not shown yet: it needs each member's radius, which a stored tree does not keep (GEN.952).

## [8.0.2559] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The cache warm-up of sector, system and phenomenon pages is cut into short units, and emptying a scatter no longer runs one statement over millions of rows.

### Changed
- **PERF.180: the three object families of the cache warm-up are slices of their listing.** `warm-sectors`, `warm-systems` and `warm-phenomena` were one unit each, minutes on a large galaxy once the cap is raised; each is now units of 250 objects (a whole multiple of that past 4,000 units), declared at 75 s against the 300 s unit ceiling. The stage leaves one line in the activity log for all its units.
- **Emptying the bright-star or phenomenon scatter removes its member and node rows in a way that cannot run for minutes in one statement.** The two tables are truncated when the other scatter has none, else the rows go in batches of 100,000 that each commit. No stored value changes; the timing on a large galaxy still has to be measured.

## [8.0.2558] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** Reset view now works after the minus button has been pressed past the end of the sector's range, where it used to do nothing.

### Fixed

- **Reset view, Fly to and Centre end a zoom-distance goal still being chased (TEST.458).** Plus and minus (and the slider and a pinch) ask for a camera distance and keep chasing it, across stages if need be, for a few seconds. Pressing minus repeatedly in an opened sector left that goal alive at the end of the sector's range; Reset view flew the camera back to the opening view and the chase then took it straight out again, so the button seemed to do nothing. A move the person asks for now ends the goal first. The scale-line browser test also took its opening zoom from a frame of the page's flight in; it now waits for the flight to land, a new test holds the Reset view case, and the MAP.301 browser test now holds that the camera comes into the dense region and rests in it rather than one resting point, which moved with the frames the approach took. No stored value or generated output changes.

## [8.0.2557] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The line after a reset now says how many tables were wiped and how many rows they held, counted, instead of "about 1 row".

### Fixed
- **UX.164: the wipe line gave the database's stale statistic ("Wiped 75 tables (about 1 row)").** `planetgen reset` and the Generate page's reset now count each table before wiping it (a table the statistics put under 200,000 rows is counted exactly in a moment) and say, for example, "Wiped 75 tables from 'galaxy' (12 tables held rows, 4,512 rows removed)", or "all were already empty" for an empty database. The few very large tables keep the statistic, as counting them row by row would take minutes, and the line says so ("... and about 9,000,000 more by the database's statistics in its large tables"). No stored value changes.

## [8.0.2556] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The plan estimate for a neighbourhood run is pinned by a test against the run that showed it wrong.

### Fixed
- **PERF.178: the plan estimate said 33 GB and 2 min 33 s for a run that took 4 min 28 s.** The pieces were already in: the galaxy-wide scatter tables are left out of the size per system (a few hundred megabytes for the 3,800 systems of that run, not 33 GB), the line no longer says "Refused ... Going ahead" (#2831), and a time worked out from the default speed reads as the range it lies within with "not timed yet on this server". A new test runs the logged case through the estimate and checks all three: the size is small, the range holds the 4 min 28 s the run took, and the summary says the time is not timed yet. No stored value changes.

## [8.0.2555] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The progress bars in a job log are guarded by a test that they are never cut off at the log's width.

### Fixed
- **PERF.179: progress bars cut off in the job log ("elapsed 0:0... remaining 0:00:...").** The cut was rich assuming 80 columns for output that is not a terminal; the bars are drawn 160 wide there (already in place). New tests render the bars to a log the way a job does and fail if the elapsed or remaining time is cut, if the line passes the log width for the longest realistic step name, count and run time, or if a terminal or a `COLUMNS` setting stops being left to rich. No stored value changes.

## [8.0.2554] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The star mass function now has a test that measures the generator's stars bin by bin in mass against the published curves.

### Added

- **A star mass function census (TEST.454).** The Galactic disk curves (Chabrier 2003's log-normal fits for single stars and for systems, Kroupa 2001's broken power law) are held as data, and a census draws 60,000 systems at the reference solar position and compares the primaries (with the system function) and every star of every system (with the single-star functions) in six mass bins from 0.08 to 0.8 solar masses. It also reports the primaries above 0.8 solar masses by phase and the white dwarfs' mean mass. It already shows two bins of the primaries off the system function (0.08 to 0.12 solar masses has 24% against 13 to 20%, 0.6 to 0.8 has 6.9% against 7.7 to 12%), tagged GEN.928; the later items of the chain are measured against it.

## [8.0.2553] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The waiting-list setting's help text no longer shows an internal item code.

### Fixed
- **The `queue.max_waiting` help text named an internal item code.** It is reworded, so no item code reaches the settings page, the config reference or the example file (TEST.457).

## [8.0.2552] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The stellar mass function now lives in one module, so the next change to it is made in one place.

### Changed

- **One initial mass function module (GEN.926).** The mass function was written out in six places (the draw and the count in the stellar evolution module, the moments in the system mass module, the stars per solar mass in the H II module, the mass a population returns in the disk history, the mass grid in the star population module). It is now `physics/imf.py`: the draw of a star's mass, the number or mass of stars in a range, the density and the segments a table is built on. Nothing generated changes (the golden output is the same); the old names are gone.

## [8.0.2551] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** Scrolling the wheel toward a dense crowd of stars now brings the camera into the crowd and stops there instead of flying through it to a star behind.

### Fixed

- **Wheel zoom heads for the most populated layer in front of the zoom direction (MAP.301).** The wheel zooms toward the thing under the pointer, and when that was a lone star behind a crowd (a cluster, a dense region) the camera passed through the crowd without stopping. The pick now also looks along the ray under the pointer for the densest layer of drawn stars in front of that thing (a bounded search over log-spaced depth slices, a narrow cone around the ray, at least twelve stars) and, where it finds one, the approach slows and ends in that layer; the next scroll carries on past it. A pointer over empty space, a lone star, a body, or a crowd smaller than twelve stars is unaffected. No stored value or generated output changes.

## [8.0.2550] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** Planet and moon pages now say how much of the time the star is up, and a moon shows the extra night in its planet's shadow.

### Added
- **UX.205: the day and night time shares on planet and moon pages.** The summary gains a sentence from the stored shares: the share of the time the star is up at the equator, the hours of daylight in each solar day, and the share over the whole surface. A world that turns once an orbit says it keeps one face to its star (a day side always lit, a terminator ring, a night side always dark). A moon in its planet's shadow adds the share of its time in that shadow and the length of the longest eclipse, which is also a new row of its rotation group (worked out from its orbit and the planet's radius, not stored). The At a glance panel lists the hours of daylight and the equator's share of daylight. An object with no rotation shows none of this.

### Changed
- **The row "Hours of daylight a person can be outside" is now "Hours a person can work outside per year (dose limit)",** which is what the stored number is. No stored value changes.

## [8.0.2549] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** In a dense area no map name overlaps or crowds another, and where names must be cut the brighter or heavier thing keeps its name.

### Fixed
- **Names stood closer than their buffer, and sometimes over each other (MAP.299).** Three causes in the label engine: the screen grid only compared names in the same cell, so two names a few pixels apart across a grid line were never compared; a name's width was measured in one font whatever its kind, though a sector's name is semibold and a nebula's italic; and a name was placed at a fractional position and drawn at a rounded one. Names are now whole pixels wide enough for their own font, the grid reaches each name's buffer, and a browser test of the fixture's densest region finds none closer than the buffer at three zooms.
- **The buffer is a setting.** `map.labelBuffer` (pixels, 0 to 40, default 4) in the browser's preferences, read at each placement.
- **Where names of one kind compete for room the brighter or heavier keeps the better place.** A star by its brightness, an object or body by its mass, a nebula by its volume; the budget still chooses which things get a name and the order between kinds is unchanged.

## [8.0.2548] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The wheel now zooms in far enough on a dense cluster to single out one star from its neighbours.

### Fixed
- **MAP.300: the mouse wheel stalled short of a star in a dense cluster.** With no sector open, the wheel only knew the stars of an open sector, so a pointer on a drawn star zoomed toward the focus plane or the column behind it and the eye stopped well short of the star. The wheel now takes any star the map draws from its nodes' lists as the thing under the pointer, so the camera comes in on it to the least distance the map allows (a thousandth of a parsec) and two stars under a tenth of a parsec apart are each the star under the pointer on their own spots. No stored value changes.

## [8.0.2547] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The class-blind life test and the prevalence tests are settled after the class cut-over (epoch 121): fixed faults lose their tags and the open ones are named.

### Changed

- **The class-blind life test samples the sweep (TEST.452).** A class letter can no longer be forced on a bare planet (it is derived from the conditions), so the generator's life step is run on the 388 planets and moons of the shared sweep and, as before, on copies put under every other class letter. It passes on epoch 121.
- **Tags settled after the cut-over (TEST.301, TEST.395, TEST.431).** The stored class equals the conditions' class on all 919 bodies, so that tag is gone and the rule is enforced. Thirteen other tags that no longer trip (mass function, hot Jupiters on M dwarfs, habitable classes, moons per planet) are removed. A request for a habitable world still goes unmet in 11 of 12 systems and is now named under GEN.909, GEN.853, GEN.854 and GEN.916. Tests and data only.

## [8.0.2546] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** A supernova remnant on the Sector Map is now drawn from its age: young ones a thin bright rim, old ones a thick faint shell.

### Changed
- **Remnant shells by age (MAP.286).** The sector scene now carries each supernova remnant's age, and the shell is painted from it: a 50-year-old remnant is a thin, bright, hot-coloured rim around a hollow centre, and a 100,000-year-old one a thick, faint, cooler shell with the hollow filling in, with every age between interpolated on a log scale. The remnant's card shows its age, and the sector API's `phenomena` entries gain `age_years` (null for other types). The look is a stand-in that follows the body-rendering design table; the filament texture and colour by emission class are still to come. Nothing generated or stored changes.

## [8.0.2545] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The warm-up no longer reports an answer built on every run for a sector page whose Profile the API refuses.

### Fixed

- **The warm-up's "answers built" counts only answers that were built (MAP.289).** The sector page of a sector with a grid address asks the API for its Profile; where the API refuses (a database with no planned galaxy answers 404) the question was counted as an answer built, and asked again on every run, so a warm run over an unchanged galaxy always read "1 built" in its objects phase instead of "unchanged, nothing built". An answer the API refuses is now counted as neither built nor cached. A galaxy with a plan already cached its Profile and is unaffected; a test now holds that for several sectors. No stored value or generated output changes.

## [8.0.2544] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** Superbubbles on the Galaxy Map now have a crisp rim and a fainter fill instead of three crossing rings.

### Changed
- **Clearer bounds and more transparency for superbubbles (MAP.236).** A bubble was three faint great circles (opacity 0.14), so its bound read as two crossing ellipses and the inside had no edge. It is now its sphere: a faint even fill (0.06 on the dark map, 0.07 on the light) and a crisp rim about two pixels wide where the sphere meets the line of sight, so the silhouette is the bound, in a lighter blue on the dark map and a darker one on the light. A camera inside a bubble, as the Sun is, sees the shell round it with no doubled layer. The look is in the new `static/superbubble.js`; no stored value changes.

## [8.0.2543] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** A planet's or moon's class is no longer drawn: every body is made from its mass, where it formed and its star, and the class letter is worked out from what it comes out as.

### Changed
generation-output: changed

- **The class cut-over (GEN.646, GEN.681, GEN.682, GEN.684, GEN.685, GEN.687, GEN.688, GEN.689, GEN.690, GEN.840, and the mass-function half of GEN.829).** A planet's mass comes from the mass law (`physics/planet_mass.py`), its kind (rocky or giant) and origin (inside or beyond the snow line) from its formation (`physics/planet_kind.py`), its radius from its structure, its water from where it formed, its air from the air solver, and its class from `classify` at the end of its build and again once its star's flux variation is known. The class tables (`PLANET_CLASS_PROBABILITIES`, the zone gates, the radius, albedo and size-mode ranges, the moon blacklist) and every draw keyed by a class letter are deleted. A moon is a rocky body whose mass follows `dN/dlogM ~ M^-0.5` up to a share of its parent's mass. A rogue planet, a pulsar's disc planet and a forced habitable world are made by the same law and classed by the same classifier. A request that names a class (a slot's `planet_class`, `FORCE_CLASS`, a habitable world) draws whole planets at the place until one is that class (`StarSystem.build_planet`), and a request no draw can meet (a white dwarf's ecosphere holds no air) is left unmet instead of redrawing the system. A caller who gives a mass or radius outside 1e12 to 2.5e28 kg and 0.5 to 200,000 km, or a density outside what a planet can have, now gets a `ValueError`.
- **Two bounds of the air solver, both stand-ins (registry rows CC7 and CC8).** The surface a greenhouse can reach stops at 2000 K, and a pressure that falls under 1 Pa is taken as an exosphere (airless); both were found by the first sweeps of the cut-over, where the iteration reached 3700 K and 1e-10 bar and the gas equilibrium did not converge. A sky colour is shown as none where an air of hundreds of kilobars leaves no light at the zenith.
- **What changes for a reader of a system.** Every planet and moon is a different draw (new masses, makes and airs), so every generated system changes. The class sweep (`tests/class_sweep_cli.py`, report `class-cutover-sweep-2026-10-28.md`) lists the shares. Class T stays rare until the envelope law of the gas dwarfs (GEN.822, Aux 17), and class N is a large share of the warm planets until Aux 8's sinks and hydrogen cap (GEN.830, GEN.837) merge.
- **Life reads conditions, not the letter.** Water share, porosity, albedo and the air no longer read a class letter (a body has class None until its conditions are final). Still keyed by the letter and filed apart: the dominant surface material (`surface_composition`), the stream label of the aerosols, the redraw of a life class in the ecosphere when `HABITABLE_WORLD` is False and the request steering by class (GEN.915, GEN.916).
- **Prevalence.** The usual `habitable_world` share is 0.722 (it counts the classes that can carry life, mostly Q, P, V and K, while few worlds are habitable by the score; GEN.911 reworks the aim). The class census is re-baselined at this code and no longer bars a class from a zone; the system census shifts are tagged GEN.646.

## [8.0.2542] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The clear-scatter test no longer fails when an earlier test left the logger silent.

### Changed
- **The test that reads the console sets the console first.** `test_clearing_a_scatter_with_nothing_stored_says_so_and_changes_nothing` read `capsys.out` but the logger belongs to the test process: a test that ran `main()` with `--quiet`, `--silent` or `--output -` (or the web app, which has no console handler) left it silent or writing to stderr, so under a parallel gate the message came back as an empty string. The module now sets the logger to write to stdout before each test. Tests only; the product is unchanged.

## [8.0.2541] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** A galaxy with more than 4,000 nebula field slabs no longer fails the nebula field stage; its units cover several slabs each.

### Changed
- **The nebula field stage cuts like the other fixed-size stages.** It queued one unit per 50 pc slab, so a galaxy wide enough for more than 4,000 slabs failed with "a stage queues at most 4000 units". Beyond that size a unit now draws a run of consecutive slabs (`units.coarsen`), the same cut at any worker count and the same clouds; below it nothing changes. The log still has a line per slab.

## [8.0.2540] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** Anything that has to wait for the machine now waits in one list, up to eight entries (a setting), and the job strip shows the order.

### Changed
- **One waiting list in Redis (PERF.154).** A generation run, an API job (a one-sector regenerate, a neighbourhood) or a Generate page job that finds the machine or the running job busy takes a place in one ordered list (`planetgen/queue/runline.py`) instead of failing with "busy" or taking the single `next.json` slot. The list holds `queue.max_waiting` entries (8 by default, on the admin settings page); one more is refused with the list named. Jobs and runs each start in the order they arrived. A script that posts to the Generate page behind a running job gets `202 {"queued": true, "position": ...}` instead of a 409.
- **The job strip shows the list.** Every waiting job and run is listed in the order it arrived with its place; a waiting job has Discard (and Start now when the job before it failed); a waiting run shows its place for the machine.
- **The Generate page's job lock moved to Redis** (`planetgen:job:active`), and a waiting job's recipe is a private file `queued-<ticket>.json` in the jobs folder (it holds the database environment, which stays out of Redis). The `active` and `next.json` files, `queue/runwait.py` and the file-lock clean-up marker are gone. The Queue page's fill buttons no longer refuse while a run is live; they wait their turn.
- No generated value changes: the list only decides when a run starts, never how its work is cut.

## [8.0.2539] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The class-blind life test now also runs the generator's life step and checks it gives life exactly where the life model says it can live, whatever the class letter is.

### Changed

## [8.0.2534] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** A world's life now belongs to one of fifteen classes, from oxygen-making plants to hydrogen eaters under the ice, and how far it gets is set by the energy and oxygen its class has to work with.

### Changed
- **The life class switch (GEN.867, GEN.889).** Every rocky body with life now stores one class (1a, 1b, 1c, 2, 3a, 3b, 4a, 4b, 4c, 5a, 5b, 6, 7, 8, 9): the class with the most net primary production among those its water, temperature, light and chemistry allow. Classes within a factor of two of each other are tied and an NPP-weighted draw picks between them. Classes 1 to 4 and 6 to 7 are drawn in this release; the acid medium of 5, 8 and 9 and the ammonia water of 8 come with GEN.888 and GEN.894. Only a class that makes free oxygen (Class 1) feeds the oxygen budget. The body keeps its likelihood for every class in `planet_life_class_scores` and `moon_life_class_scores` (schema v175).
- **What a chemical class eats, as supplies (GEN.887).** `physics/life_supply.py` works out hydrogen from serpentinisation and radiolysis, reduced gas and iron, nitrate and perchlorate, and the haze organics of a methane sea from the columns a body already stores. The subsurface classes read the temperature of their own water (`habitat_temperature_k`: the base of an ice lid, or the aquifer's rise with depth) and not the surface's.
- **The complexity index and the animal grades (GEN.890, GEN.877, GEN.882 to GEN.884).** A class reaches complex cells, multicellular bodies and animals of grade A1 (sessile), A2 (small mobile) and A3 (large, active) when its index C (net primary production over the Earth's, times the yield of what it breathes, times the temperature rate factor) passes a threshold; an oxygen breather also needs the oxygen of the grade (0.1, 2 and 6 kPa). A civilization needs A3. A few anoxic worlds get animals that have lost aerobic respiration (route R4, GEN.884). Chemosymbiotic animals under the ice (Class 4) come out of the same rule.
- **A body's life draws from its own stream (GEN.872).** The life rolls of one body no longer move the rolls of the next body, so an edit of one planet leaves the others as they were.
- **Class words everywhere (GEN.892, GEN.869).** The planet and moon pages, the system sheet, the search page, the system map and the population pass name the class and its stage in the class's own words (`life_class_text`), and the object page shows the class, the best class that could live there, the animal grade and the complexity.
- **The toxic gases of the table reach the world (GEN.657).** Ammonia, hydrogen fluoride, hydrogen chloride, chlorine, nitrogen dioxide, hydrogen cyanide and ozone now count in the gas filter and the corrosive test, as CO, H2S and SO2 did.
- **Every constant has a registry row (GEN.893).** `tuning.LIFE_COMPLEXITY`, `tuning.LIFE_NPP`, the supply numbers and the habitat temperature numbers carry tiers and tweak levels in `docs/design/research/stand-in-values.md`.

generation-output: changed

## [8.0.2532] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** A generation run that stopped partway can be finished instead of wiped: `planetgen finish-run`, or "Finish the last run" on the Generate page.

### Added
- **Finish the last run.** A run that was killed, ran out of database memory or was cancelled carries on from the first stage that did not finish, on the same galaxy: the stages it finished are kept, the stage that stopped runs again from its start (a sector stage skips the sectors it already saved, a scatter empties what it rewrites first), and every stage after it runs as it would have. The galaxy ends the same as an uninterrupted run (same seed, same sectors, same scatter).
- **Where.** `planetgen finish-run [--run ID]`, the "Finish the last run" card on the Generate page (it also goes on with the steps of that job that never started, for example the link and the sector paths of a New galaxy), and the typed command `finish run`. A failed run now prints the `planetgen finish-run` line.
- **Safe.** A run records the galaxy's seed and the PlanetGen build it worked on, and is carried on only while both are still the ones it started on, in the database it worked on. A run is carried on once; a finish that stops is finished in turn.

### Changed
- **The run record keeps what each stage finished**, and the starting run's galaxy seed, build and the run it carried on. The Queue page's Retry is unchanged.

## [8.0.2531] - 2026-10-29

**Headline:** The Galaxy Map's near-sector request no longer fails with a server error for a point very far away, and the galaxy generation tests run in half an hour less.

### Fixed
- **`/galaxy/near` answered 500 for a point 1e200 parsecs away.** The distance from the centre was found by squaring the three coordinates, which overflows a float for a coordinate that large; it uses the overflow-safe hypotenuse now, and a point that far gets the normal empty answer. Regression tests cover three far points (TEST.451).
- **`test_galaxy_gen.py` took half an hour and stopped single tests at the 900 s limit.** Its sparse-wedge test generated a dense sector with every system's planets, moons and solved air (the "settle-job timeout" Core 5 saw). These tests are about which sectors a run makes and where, so the whole file now makes planetless systems; it runs in 18 minutes and its slowest test takes 7 (TEST.451).
