## [8.0.2318] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** The planet generator now has a model of the volatiles that late impacts deliver to a rocky planet and the air they blow away.

### Changed
- **Impact erosion and late delivery (GEN.739).** A new module (`impact_history`) takes the mass a rocky planet accretes after its giant impacts (0.7 percent of an Earth mass for the Earth, falling with mass), the water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen those impactors bring, and the air they erode, and returns what the air and the surface keep. It reproduces the Earth's nitrogen and ocean, Venus's nitrogen, and the result that late impacts alone do not make Mars thin. The supply law has a hook (`impact_inventory`) that turns the result into atoms per 100 g of mantle. Nothing in the generator calls it yet (it waits on GEN.411 and GEN.422), so no stored value changes today.
- The nine new constants are in the stand-in registry (GEN.725) with their source tier and tweak level. The design note is `docs/design/composition/impact-erosion-and-late-delivery.md`.

## [8.0.2317] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** The redox of a rocky world's magma ocean now follows the published ranges: its spread grows with mass, it keeps rising above one Earth mass, and the later mantle is never more reduced than the ocean it came from.

### Changed
- **Width and rise above one Earth mass (GEN.482b).** The spread of the magma-ocean redox grows from 0.5 log units at 0.1 Earth masses to 0.9 at one (the Hirschmann 2022 and Deng 2020 ranges for the Moon, Mars and Earth), and the mean keeps rising by 1.0 per dex of mass up to 5.4 Earth masses, where the pressures of the published calculations end. Nothing in the generator draws the mixture yet (it waits on GEN.411 and GEN.422), so no stored value changes today; the first air of a heavier rocky world will be more oxidised than before once it does.
- **The later mantle (GEN.482b).** Its mean is held at the Earth value above one Earth mass (no source goes further), and a body never moves to a later mantle more reduced than its own magma-ocean surface.
- Rows a1 and a2 are listed as partly verified with their limits (GEN.482); row a3 is unchanged because nothing reads it for a body with an air.

## [8.0.2316] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** The gas table now holds K2, KO, K2O, Na2O and Al, so the vapour over a lava world lists the alkali oxides it makes instead of dropping them.

### Added
- **Lava-vapour gases (GEN.751).** K2, KO, K2O and Na2O, and Al, are in the NASA thermodynamic table (94 species) and the gas table (108 gases), computed from the NASA fits like the other lava-vapour species. A lava-world draw lists the four alkali species it makes (KO is about 4e-7 bar over a bulk-silicate-Earth melt at 2500 K); aluminium is in the table but the melt model has no aluminium activity yet, so none is drawn. The mixture draw is not called by the generator yet, so no generated value changes.

### Fixed
- **A K2 star is not the potassium dimer.** The text that marks chemical formulas no longer reads the spectral type "K2" as the gas K2, which the table now holds; the `formula` filter still writes K2 out where it is named.

## [8.0.2315] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** A dry, frozen or hot world can now hold liquid water underground, which lifts its Water rating and lets microbes live there.

### Changed
- **Aquifers (GEN.654, DB.92, schema v157).** A rocky world or moon with no liquid at its surface keeps `aquifer_depth_km` and `aquifer_thickness_km`, worked out by `physics/aquifers.py` from its heat flow, its surface temperature and pressure, its gravity and the water left in its surface reservoir: the layer of its crust where the pores are open and the water is liquid and not hotter than life can use. A world with none, a gas giant and a galaxy made earlier keep NULL (migration 0156).
- **What it does to the score.** The water is a solvent for life (the Microbial score can rise, capped at abiogenesis, so Flora, Fauna and Sentient stay 0), the life sees the ground's dose and the chemical power of the heat flow, and the Water rung is Yellow when the layer starts within 5 km and Red when it is deeper. A world with an ocean at the surface has none. The property sheet lists both numbers.
- Every parameter is a labelled DESIGN stand-in (`tuning.py`, `DATA-LICENSE.md`); the generator epoch is bumped because worlds that had no life now draw a chemistry.

**Headline:** Pages get an "On this page" contents list, and every page is checked for a clean heading outline.

- Every page with three or more sections shows an "On this page" list after its title, built from its headings; following an entry into a collapsed section opens it (UX.196).
- The accessibility suite now fails a page with more than one h1, a skipped heading level, or a table with no heading, caption or label (UX.195).

## [8.0.2305] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** `planetgen sector` and `planetgen phenomenon` now only generate; the population pass and the sector paths are commands of their own.

### Changed
- **`sector` no longer takes `--population` (PERF.124).** A `sector` run saves its sectors and stops; the population pass is `planetgen population`, or a stage of a `galaxy` run.
- **`phenomenon` no longer saves sector paths, and `--no-settle` is gone (PERF.124).** `planetgen phenomenon --sector-id N` saves the phenomenon and nothing else.

### Added
- **`planetgen settle --sector-id ID...`.** Saves the paths of the named sectors and the sectors around them (the step that follows `phenomenon --sector-id` for a black hole or neutron star); it takes the place of `--since` and the two cannot be combined.

## [8.0.2304] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** `scripts/test.py` checks MySQL, Redis and the test setup before a run, restarts a server that dies during it and carries on without redoing the tests that passed; `full` is no longer called the merge gate.

### Added
- **A check before every run (TEST.376).** `scripts/test.py` loads the `PLANETGEN_TEST_*` variables from `/etc/profile.d/planetgen-test.sh` when they are missing, starts MySQL and Redis when they do not answer, purges the MySQL binary logs when under 3 GB of disk is free, and checks `argon2-cffi` and `playwright` 1.56.0. What it cannot repair stops the run with `PREFLIGHT FAILED: ...` and exit 2. `scripts/test.py env` does only the check; `--no-preflight` skips it. Before this a database test with MySQL down was skipped, not failed, and a run without `PLANETGEN_TEST_MYSQL_USER` failed with `DatabaseLoginError` as the wrong account.
- **A watchdog during every run.** MySQL and Redis are asked every 15 seconds. A server that is gone is restarted, the phase's pytest is stopped and started again without the tests that already passed (the progress log, as `--resume` does), up to 5 times a phase; the closing line says how many restarts there were. A server that cannot be restarted ends the run with `FAIL` and exit 3, and `--resume` continues it.

### Changed
- **`full` is the end-of-version run, not the merge gate (TEST.372).** The help of `scripts/test.py` and docs/reference/testing.md now say an ordinary merge needs a green `changed` run (finished with `--resume` after an interruption), and that the whole suite is for TEST.261, SEC.33 and GEN.301.

TODO items resolved: TEST.372, TEST.376. Added: none.

## [8.0.2303] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** The update reloads the web server more safely: it tests Apache's configuration first, covers gunicorn hosts, and checks the site answers.

### Changed
- **`update.sh` reload (OPS.29).** Apache is checked with `apache2ctl configtest` before it is reloaded, so a broken config leaves the running Apache serving; it is restarted only when the update just installed or enabled mod_wsgi (other modules load on a reload). The `planetgen-gunicorn` unit (Linux) and the launchd gunicorn daemon (macOS) are reloaded the same way, and `/api/health` must answer afterwards (`PLANETGEN_HEALTH_URL` sets another address). A failed step ends the update non-zero and prints the command to run by hand; nothing running prints the commands and ends zero. The docs (`apache.md`, the server checklist) say a reload aborts requests a mod_wsgi daemon is serving after about 4 seconds.

## [8.0.2301] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** An account can have a picture, and it may be a GIF, an animated GIF too, checked under frame and pixel caps and stored as a clean copy.

### Added
- **Your picture (SEC.36).** The account page has a "Your picture" section to upload or remove a PNG, JPEG, ICO or GIF, and the picture shows beside "Signed in as". `POST /api/auth/avatar` and `DELETE /api/auth/avatar` do the same for the API, and `GET /api/auth/me` returns the picture's address. Control schema v20 adds `admin_users.avatar` (the update adds the column).
- **The avatar rules.** At most 1 MiB, 1024 by 1024 pixels a frame, 100 frames, and 16 million pixels over all the frames. A GIF or PNG with several frames stays animated with its durations and loop count. The upload is refused in a plain sentence when it is over a cap, is a bomb header, or is another format.

### Security
- **A GIF is read only for an account picture, and never from the uploaded bytes.** Pillow is told which four formats to try, the size is read from the header before anything is decoded, a decompression-bomb warning is an error, `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` is lowered to 25 million, and frames are unpacked one at a time under the caps. What is stored is Pillow's new encoding of the pixels, so comments, XMP, ICC profiles, EXIF and application extensions other than the loop block do not survive. It is served with its own content type and `nosniff`. The site logo, icons and preview picture keep the SEC.35 rule and still refuse a GIF.

## [8.0.2292] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** A server with no timing history now shows a rough time left, labelled as a guess, instead of "estimating".

### Fixed
- **Time estimates broke on a server that had never timed a stage (PERF.184).** A run's time left, the banner's
  hours and the Generate page's whole-job bar said "estimating" until a first unit finished, and left a later stage out
  of the total. They now start from a rough guess: the stage's units over the workers the host can run at once (its
  cores and memory) at a default cost per unit. The guess is labelled "rough guess" with a wide range (0.4 to 3 times the
  figure), the sector estimate says "anywhere from A to B" while its speed is the default, and each figure is replaced
  by the run's own pace as units finish.
- **A stage with no stored history now learns.** When a stage of a queue run ends, its time and its cost per worker second
  are folded into a running average (`queue/stagetimes.py`), so the next run of the warm-up and the fills starts from
  what the last one took, and the estimate tightens run after run.

## [8.0.2285] - 2026-10-25

**Headline:** The plan's "about N stars expected" for the massive-star and bright-star passes now matches what the passes place, and each unit line says the stars it expects.

### Changed
- **The expected-stars count beyond the outline follows the density (GEN.398, bug).** The count of stars a shell holds beyond the galaxy's outline (what the pass's log line, its progress bar and its ETA use) probed each group at two longitudes 180 degrees apart. On a two-armed spiral both land on the same phase of the arms, so a group's young stars came out twice, or none, of what the sampler draws: on the default galaxy the shells just past the outline were counted at 3,250 stars where the pass placed 1,853. A group is now sampled at 8 colatitudes and 2 radii of equal volume and 16 longitudes, so its count follows the density wherever the disc falls away across it. On the default galaxy (4e9 solar masses, seed 0123...) the massive-star pass logged 22,593 and placed 21,642 before; it counts 21,389 now, and the part beyond the outline matches the stars placed in each range of shells within 4 percent. The sampler was right and is unchanged: no star moves and no generator epoch is spent.
- **A unit line says the stars it expects, not its weight.** The "unit 8 of 445, about 133 stars expected" lines gave the unit's weight, its stars plus a share for every band walked, so a unit that placed 19 said it expected 133. They give the stars the unit is expected to place.
- **Tests.** The count beyond the outline matches a Monte Carlo of the density within 6 percent for six shells of the toy galaxy; a task's expected stars are its shells', the far shells' or the components' share, not its weight.

## [8.0.2277] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The picture upload now reads only PNG, JPEG and ICO files, and Pillow moves to 13.0.0, which fixes 37 reported flaws in its image decoders.

### Security
- **Pillow 12.3.0 to 13.0.0 in both lock files (SEC.34).** `pip-audit` listed 37 advisories for 12.3.0, all fixed in 13.0.0 (TIFF, GIF and PPM decoders reading out of bounds, a zero-width PPM, PDF appends). Only the pillow pin moved in `requirements.lock` and `requirements-server.lock`; the picture tests and the lock tests pass on 13.0.0.
- **The admin picture upload asks Pillow for PNG, JPEG and ICO only (SEC.35).** It used to let Pillow try every format it knows and reject all but three afterwards, so a TIFF, GIF or PPM header was parsed first. `Image.open` now gets `formats=` the three, so a file of any other kind is "That file is not a readable picture." and no other decoder runs. New cases in `test_web_seo.py` refuse a TIFF, a GIF and a PPM.

## [8.0.2276] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Every call to the API now leaves one line in the activity log with who made it, how it came in, the route and the HTTP response code.

### Changed
- **Every `/api/` request is logged (API.15).** `planetgen.log` gets an `API call` line when the answer is ready: the account (the key's owner, the signed-in user, `god` for a command-line tool, or `-`), `via=` (`key`, `session`, `anonymous`, `console`), method, route, path, HTTP status, milliseconds, bytes in and out, the user agent and the API version the client sent. Keys, tokens, passwords and bodies are never written.
- **`X-Request-Id`.** Each answer carries the request id that is in the log line; a client's own well-formed id is kept.
- **`api_log.internal`.** The calls the web pages make in-process (about six per page view) are marked `internal=1`; setting this to `off` leaves them out of the log. Default `all`.
- The command-line tools that lift a lockout, forget devices and reset two-factor write the same line with `user="god"` and `via=console`.

## [8.0.2270] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Two small parts that let the generator call the atmosphere mixture draw are in: the description of a body it reads, and what an ocean takes out of the drawn air.

### Added

## [8.0.2269] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Cold icy worlds now trap gas in ice cages, and cold dry worlds can keep liquid brine below the freezing point of water.

### Changed
- **Hydrate cages in the atmosphere (GEN.762).** An icy body under 273 K holds CO2, CO, N2, CH4 and H2S above their clathrate dissociation pressure in the water cages of its ice skin (depth drawn from 1 m to 1 km, a stand-in); the held gas leaves the air, so some cold icy moons now have thinner air.
- **Brine under the ice (GEN.762).** A cold body with very little surface water melts the base of its ice at the eutectic of a perchlorate brine (198 to 236 K) instead of 273 K, so it can keep a liquid brine ocean under a thin lid or none, with that salt's water activity.

## [8.0.2267] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The phenomena scatter no longer holds gigabytes in one process, and the block light totals at its end show their progress instead of going quiet.

### Changed
- **The block light totals are written as they are complete (PERF.187).** `db.block_lights.rebuild` kept every block of a unit of 729 sector shells in memory until the unit ended; on a 12 pc galaxy that was the scatter step's 6.4 GB (7.9 GB measured while the step ran). It now reads one shell at a time and writes a block as soon as the shells have passed it, so what it holds is the blocks of the current block shell of each level.
- **The nebula block totals write one level at a time (PERF.187).** `galaxy.nebula_blocks.iter_rows` gives the levels one by one and lets go of a level's cover once its rows are made; `db.nebula_blocks.rebuild` writes each level as it comes instead of holding the rows of all of them. `all_rows` still returns the dict for the callers that want it.
- **The block light totals report their progress (PERF.189, Boss).** After the hypervelocity stars' epoch is stamped, a scatter used to go quiet while the map's block light totals were made. They are now a step of their own ("Making the block light totals", bar over the units), with a log line before the scan, after it, before the levels above the units and about every 30 seconds (`tuning.PROGRESS_LOG_SECONDS`).
- **The smoke budget for the scatter step is lowered (PERF.187)** to the new measured peak.
- **The logging standard has the rule for work after a progress block (DOC.80):** it needs a step of its own, with a short checklist.

## [8.0.2260] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The Galaxy Map keeps its stars in one buffer that each node adds to as it arrives, and positions are exact however far from the galaxy's centre the camera is.

### Changed
- **One star buffer, filled node by node (MAP.267).** A node arriving writes its own stars at the end of the star buffer and a node leaving is cut out by moving the tail of the buffer into its place; the nodes already drawn are not touched, where every change of the view used to rebuild every star (`static/starbuffer.js`, `SlotStore`). The buffer doubles when it is full. A change of the star filters still starts it afresh.
- **Stars are placed relative to the eye (MAP.267).** Each position is a high and a low float32 and the shader subtracts the camera's own pair, so a star keeps under a quarter pixel down to about 0.2 AU from the camera at any distance from the galaxy's centre (one float32 was a dozen pixels off a parsec away 260 kpc out). The old frame rounded to a whole parsec at the camera's target is gone. The other browser buffers (territory dots, superbubbles, rings, block prisms, the system view) are still absolute: they stay with MAP.240.

## [8.0.2259] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The surface pressure of a rocky world now has a physical law behind it: how much gas its interior has delivered by its age and what the ocean and the carbonate-silicate cycle take back, calibrated on the Earth and checked on Venus.

### Changed
- **The supply law of the surface pressure (GEN.726).** `physics/surface_pressure.py` gives the pieces the pressure sum of GEN.422 will use: the share of the mantle's volatiles that the body's heat release has brought to the surface (`degassed_share`, the melt-processing picture of Tosi et al. 2017, one calibrated energy so that an Earth twin has the Earth's 1e22 mol of surface carbon), the gas mass and pressure of a degassed budget, and the CO2 pressure at which silicate weathering balances volcanic outgassing (`carbonate_pco2_bar`, the law and the ranges of Lehmer, Catling and Krissansen-Totton 2020, solved with the surface temperature as a function of the pressure). `interior_heat.Heat` also reports the heat the interior has released since the body formed (`released_j`). Nothing is wired into the generator yet (GEN.411 and GEN.422 do that), so no world changes. The design is `docs/design/composition/surface-pressure-supply-law.md`; the seven stand-in constants are registry rows AM27 to AM33.

## [8.0.2258] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A world's air is now stored gas by gas in its own tables, so any gas of the gas table can be in an atmosphere and the balance gas of a giant (helium) or a hot world (sodium) is a stored gas like the rest.

### Changed
- **The air moves to `planet_gases` and `moon_gases` (DB.71, GEN.424).** The ten `p_<gas>_kpa` columns of `planets` and `moons` are gone. Each gas above zero is a row (the formula in the gas table and its partial pressure in Pa), the class's balance gas (helium, sodium, ammonia) included, so the rows add up to the surface pressure. Migration 0155 copies each row's ten partial pressures into the new tables and drops the columns (schema 155); a row made before it has no balance-gas row until the galaxy is regenerated. `physics/atmosphere.py` keeps the air as the body attribute `gas_partials_pa`; `physics/mixture.py`, `physics/air_column.py`, the habitability, class, radiation, hydrosphere and System Map code read it through `atmosphere.gas_partials_pa` / `atmosphere.partial_kpa`. The System Map's body rows and the describer carry the air by gas formula. Sodium has no Rayleigh cross section, so the air column leaves it out.

## [8.0.2257] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The test gate runs the tests that start real queue workers one at a time and cuts its worker count to the memory and idle cores the machine has.

### Changed
- **`scripts/test.py` runs three phases instead of two (TEST.344).** The tests that need no browser and no real queue worker run on every core; the `real_queue` tests, which start real worker processes and read the shared queues by name (so two at once kill each other's workers, TEST.302), run on one worker; the browser tests run last on two. The phase lines show the new phase.
- **The parallel phases are capped by free memory and load.** At the start of a phase the runner counts one worker per 1000 MB of available memory (browser workers 2500 MB) and, in the first phase, no more than the cores the load leaves idle, never fewer than one, and says so on the phase line when it cuts. A lane machine that runs other lanes' gates now gets fewer workers instead of timeouts and OOM kills. `--worker-mb`, `--browser-worker-mb` and `--no-worker-cap` tune or turn it off.

## [8.0.2255] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A planet past its star's runaway greenhouse limit while the star was young now loses water, and the limit itself depends on the planet's mass.

### Changed
- **The runaway greenhouse limit depends on the planet's mass (GEN.639).** `orbits.runaway_greenhouse_flux` and `orbits.hz_limits` take the three Kopparapu et al. 2014 sets (0.1, 1 and 5 Earth masses): a heavier planet keeps its water to a higher flux, so its inner edge is nearer the star. The star's own habitable zone and a planet's zone label are unchanged (the zone is needed before the planet's mass is known).
- **Early water loss (GEN.639).** `physics/runaway_history.py` follows each rocky planet's and moon's flux from 30 Myr to its star's age, along the pre-main-sequence track and the star's rise to its present light, and where the flux is above the runaway limit it removes the water that the energy-limited escape of the steam takes (efficiency 0.01, the star's own XUV). `hydrosphere.generate_hydrosphere` takes the loss off the surface reservoir first, and volcanism returns 30 percent of the mantle's water, never more than was lost (the escape does not reach the mantle). The bulk water of the composition is unchanged: the loss is in the surface water, the oceans and their depth. A Sun-like star's zone loses nothing; only the worst red dwarf zones (the faintest stars and the inner edge) come out dry. Nothing new is drawn. Generator epoch bumped.

## [8.0.2251] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The old queue executor is removed; nothing in a run used it any more.

### Changed
- **The old work-queue executor is gone (OPS.66, Boss).** `WorkQueue`, `RQExecutor`, `RQFuture`, `Channel`, `_rq_task` and the `--debug FILE` plumbing of that path had no caller in a run since runs became units queued by the wrapper; nothing is kept for compatibility. ## [8.0.2250] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A Generate run no longer dies with "Execution not found in Redis" after its sectors are saved.

### Changed
- **A new-galaxy run on a loaded server failed after saving its first sectors with `ValueError: Execution ... not found in Redis` (PERF.173, bug).** A worker works out what a unit reads from the galaxy (PERF.146's warm) before it forks the unit's process, and it did that after RQ had created the unit's execution record, which expires 90 s after its last beat while the process's first beat comes 30 s after the fork. A warm of over a minute (five workers building the shape of a galaxy with 15,000 clusters at once) left a unit that finished within 30 s of the fork without its record, and RQ failed the finished unit when it cleaned up, which ended the run with its sectors saved. The worker now warms before the record is made. A unit that is already done when RQ fails it no longer fails the run or runs again, since its result is stored and counted. The note in the units' module that RQ calls `on_failure` only after the retry was wrong (RQ calls it on every failure); it now says what happens.

## [8.0.2249] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A giant's layered interior is now saved with the world and read back with it.

Its layers (kind, state, pressure and radius at the top and bottom, and the mass of each material) are saved one row per layer in two new tables, `planet_interior_layers` and `moon_interior_layers`. Worlds saved before this version have no interior until the galaxy is regenerated at the generator epoch. Database version 154.

## [8.0.2248] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The Galaxy Map shows the light of the stars too far away to tell apart as a soft glow that turns into stars as you zoom in, and the Menu can switch it off.

### Added
- **The unresolved glow (MAP.266).** Each sector-block node lists only its brightest stars; the rest of its light, stored in its aggregate (the pre-placed stars nothing was built from and the generated sectors' total), is drawn as one soft blob at the centre of that light, in the color of its temperature, under the stars. A blob shows for the share the cut gives its node (`galaxynodecut.weightCalculator`), so as a block hands over to its children the glow gives way to their stars and blobs and the light is conserved: nothing pops and nothing doubles. `static/galaxyglow.js` chooses the blobs and how strongly each shows (a tone curve over its apparent magnitude, judged 5 magnitudes deeper than a point of light); `static/galaxyglowlayer.js` draws them as screen-sized quads. The Menu's "Show on the map" group has an "Unresolved glow" button (on by default; `hide=glow` in the address turns it off). The Sector Map has no glow.
- A second warm-up over addressed sectors builds no answer (MAP.289: the bug does not reproduce; the test holds it).

## [8.0.2247] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The gas giant density test no longer fails on about one run in six, and the slow scatter-pass tests get a timeout that fits a loaded machine.

### Fixed
- **`test_gas_giant_density_is_its_mass_over_its_volume` failed in 7 of 40 runs, with or without load (the load flakes noted on TEST.344).** Since GEN.460 a giant's radius comes from the interior tables, and a hot young giant swells past 1.3 times the median mass-radius relation (one draw gave 46,695 km against a 32,741 km ceiling), so the test's 3-sigma band around the median was wrong. The test now checks the radius stays in the class's radius range and that the density is the mass over the volume; the 60 reruns after the change all pass.
- **`test_star_scatter_passes.py` runs the 900 s default timeout close on a loaded machine.** Its three scatter runs build the bright-star tables in pure Python (60 to 130 s alone), so the module now carries the same 3600 s timeout `test_budget_queries.py` uses.

## [8.0.2246] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The population model, the tuning table and the body-look pressure convert milliparsecs, megayears and pascals through the one unit registry, with the same numbers.

### Changed
- `population/model.py` (system and capital positions from milliparsecs to parsecs), `tuning.py` (the open-cluster age windows from megayears to gigayears) and `web/maps/bodylook.py` (pressure from pascals to kilopascals) call `unit_registry.converter` instead of a typed `/ 1000.0` (GEN.571, fifth file group). Each replaced expression gives the same float bit for bit, so no generated value moves. The `web/maps/starmap.py` sites use `physics.units` helpers and wait for the epoch-changing pass.

## [8.0.2245] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Moons now have an origin, and a moon caught from elsewhere can orbit backwards or steeply tilted.

### Changed
- **A moon draws how it came to orbit its planet, and its orbit follows from that (GEN.714).** A giant planet's moon is a disk moon or a captured body, a terrestrial planet's an impact moon or a captured body, and a dwarf planet's a partner or a captured body, each with an equal chance because no source gives the shares. A regular moon lies within 25 degrees of its planet's equator as before. A captured moon takes any orbit outside the band between 55 and 130 degrees where such orbits are unstable, so it is either prograde or retrograde, about 43 and 57 percent. The origin is held while the system is generated and is stored once the composition columns (DB.70) exist.

Admins see those options disabled with the reason; the Owner whose password is older sees a panel that asks for it. `GET /api/admin/settings` adds `reauth`, and an option's `fixed_kind` can be `reauth`. ## [8.0.2242] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A real Stop everything: one button, one command and one update option end every run, queue and worker process on the server and keep it quiet until you resume.

### Added
- **PERF.186: Stop everything.** The admin Queue page has a Stop everything button (and `planetgen queue stop-all` the same on the command line). It cancels the Generate page's job and every live run, empties every queue, and ends every planetgen worker, job runner and command process on the server together with the processes they started. It also writes a hold that survives a restart of Redis, the web server and the host: while it is on, no worker, run, Generate job, orbital update or cache warm-up starts, the map queues no background work, and a banner on every admin page says so. Resume (the button, or `planetgen queue resume`) lifts it. It works when Redis is not answering.
- **PERF.186: `./update.sh --kill-all`.** Runs the same stop and clear before the update, only when you give it. It leaves no hold behind.

### Fixed
- **PERF.186: Cancel left work running.** A job whose runner had died (killed by the memory killer, a restart) showed as interrupted and Cancel did nothing, while its step and the processes of that step went on using the host. Cancel now ends them, cancels the job's runs and frees the job lock. A running step that ignores the request to stop (it caught the signal or hung in a database call) is now killed after 20 seconds.
- **PERF.185: the process list was read cut off to the terminal's width** where the terminal sets one, so a worker whose command line was long could be missed by the host cap. It is now read in full, here and in the memory watch.

## [8.0.2241] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Every Generate job log now says how much memory each step used, and a nightly small New galaxy run fails when a step uses far more than its budget.

### Added
- **PERF.183: memory per step in every job log.** While a Generate job runs, the job runner looks every two seconds at MySQL, the planetgen workers, the step's own processes and the whole host, and after each step writes one line to the job log ("Memory peak: MySQL 884 MB, 6 workers 2,310 MB, the step itself 256 MB, the whole host 3,100 of 15,990 MB.") and keeps the figures in `memory.json` in the job folder. The figures are proportional set sizes, so a work horse forked from its worker is not counted twice.
- **PERF.183: the nightly New galaxy smoke run.** `python -m planetgen.cli.smoke` runs the real New galaxy job for one small neighborhood in scratch databases (dropped afterwards), prints the peaks of every step against their budgets (`tuning.SMOKE_BUDGET_MB`, or `--budget GROUP=MB`) and exits 1 when a step is over, 2 when a step failed. `examples/maintenance/install-maintenance-timer.sh --with-smoke-timer` installs a systemd timer for it at 04:30 every night, so a change that makes a step hold far more memory is caught the night it merges, not on the first big galaxy.
- **PERF.183: the first measured run found a hog.** On a 12 pc neighborhood every step stayed under 1 GB (most of them under 300 MB in their own process) except the phenomena scatter, whose own process held 6.4 GB (host 8.7 GB). Its budget is set 1.4 times that so it cannot get worse until it is fixed; every other step is judged against about twice its measured peak.

## [8.0.2236] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The Galaxy Map now draws the sector-block nodes by their size on screen and the cube tiles are gone, so a zoom no longer swaps one set of tiles for another.

### Changed
- **The map draws nodes, not cube tiles (MAP.261).** `static/galaxynodecut.js` (twin of `planetgen.galaxy.nodecut`) picks the blocks to fetch and draw by projected size: a block opens into its children as it grows on screen, between 70 and 140 px, inside the cone the camera looks along and a budget of nodes, nearest first. Each node has a weight that its ancestors' hand-over leaves it, a block whose children are not yet loaded keeps all of its weight, and `starfade.js` shows a star at the weight of the node that lists it, so a parent and its children always add up to one and a star never dips while the children arrive. The page fetches the children of what it shows before they are needed (still camera, at most 12 nodes, header `X-Map-Prefetch`) and holds nodes in IndexedDB `planetgen-nodes` and in local storage under `planetgen:node:`.

### Removed
- **Cube tiles (MAP.262).** `GET /galaxy/tiles`, `GET /api/galaxy/tiles`, `viewport.distance_cut_tiles` and its twin `galaxytilecut.js`, the tile read in `db/query.py`, the tile-keyed cache files and the tile entries of the change feed (`/api/galaxy/changes` no longer has `tiles`; it has `nodes`). ### Fixed

## [8.0.2230] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Neutron stars and black holes now have the accreting companions astronomers see: high-mass and low-mass X-ray binaries, microquasars, spider millisecond pulsars and compact triples, each with an X-ray luminosity under its Eddington limit.

### Added
- **High-mass X-ray binaries.** 40% of the compact companions of living massive stars accrete; 60% of those are Be/X-ray binaries (young systems only), the rest wind-fed supergiant binaries.
- **Low-mass X-ray binaries.** 5e-5 of neutron stars and 1e-3 of black holes have a low-mass star on a tight orbit, and 1% of those accrete from a donor filling its lobe at a period of 4 to 24 hours.
- **Microquasars.** One in ten accreting neutron stars and black holes launches jets (new member flag `microquasar`).
- **Spider millisecond pulsars.** Recycled pulsars have black widow (6%), redback (3%) and other (2%) companions with the observed masses and periods of hours (new member flag `ablating`).
- **X-ray luminosity.** A tree derives the luminosity of each accreting pair from the gas it captures, never above the accretor's Eddington limit.
- **Dormant companions and compact triples.** Detached neutron star and black hole pairs with a star are listed as dormant (the Gaia kind), and 30% of neutron star and black hole binaries now have a third member (black holes only before).

### Changed
- **Generated systems change.** A neutron star or black hole pair no longer accretes by chance geometry; the recycled pulsar companion odds follow the registry classes. Every galaxy regenerates differently (generator epoch recorded).

## [8.0.2224] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A planet's inner heat is now the heat its rock makes plus the heat it was born with, so a young world is much hotter than an old one and no longer a fixed share radiogenic.

### Changed
- **Formation heat modelled (GEN.699).** `planetgen.physics.interior_heat` follows a body's mantle from its making: it starts as hot as the energy of assembling the body allows (a magma ocean for a planet, cold for a planetesimal), then cools by convection through the mantle's boundary layer while its radioactive rock (the stored potassium, thorium, uranium and aluminium-26 of GEN.459) heats it. It is the stagnant-lid model of Guimond, Rudge and Shorttle 2022. The heat out is the radiogenic heat plus the cooling of the interior.
- **The Urey ratio is an output.** It is no longer drawn between 0.1 and 0.9; it is the radiogenic share of the heat that comes out. An Earth-mass twin gives 27 to 37 TW and a ratio of 0.57 to 0.76 over the published range of mantle rheologies, and a body of 0.1 billion years gives four to thirty times more heat than at 4.5.
- **Stored (schema 153).** `planets` and `moons` gain `mantle_eta0_pa_s` and `mantle_activation_kj_mol` (the two draws of the mantle's rheology) and `internal_heat_flux_w_m2` (the heat flow at the body's surface); `urey_ratio` keeps its column and is now computed. NULL on rows made before this release.
- The heat flow of every rocky planet, moon and rogue changes, and with it the ice shell, the ocean, the volcanism gate and the habitability score that read it.
- Generator epoch bump (numbered at merge).

## [8.0.2221] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Where an atmosphere freezes out is now worked out from the checked saturation curves, so hydrogen sulphide, carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide land at the right temperatures.

### Changed
- **The freeze-out cap reads the checked saturation curves (GEN.452).** `physics/atmosphere.py` no longer carries the two-point condensation table, whose hydrogen sulphide row was a copy of sulphur dioxide's and which put carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide and the cold gases 2 to 20 K off. The most a gas can be vapour at the surface temperature is now its saturation pressure from `physics/saturation.py` (the Fray and Schmitt and laboratory solid curves, the Span and Wagner carbon dioxide curve, the Wagner liquid curves, nothing above the critical temperature). Hydrogen sulphide boils at 213 K at 100 kPa instead of 263 K, nitrogen at 37 K holds 1.2 Pa (Pluto's air) instead of 10 Pa, and the cold gases follow the laboratory curves of the cold ends. New `saturation.condensation_temperature_k` gives the inverse. The cloud condensation of `physics/aerosols.py` reads the same curves. Stored partial pressures and total surface pressures change for cold bodies.

## [8.0.2220] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The server now refuses to run more worker processes than its memory and cores can hold, whatever starts them.

### Added
- **PERF.185: a cap on all planetgen worker processes on one host.** A start of a worker for any queue is refused once the host already runs `queue.max_host_workers` of them (0, the default, sizes it from the host: 60 percent of its memory in workers of 300 MB each, no more than four a core, never fewer than the cores plus four; a 16 GB, 8 core host gets 31). The count comes from the process list, so a worker still importing its libraries counts. The refusal is logged once a minute and counted, and the Queue page shows the cap, how many run and how many starts were refused in the last hour. This is the second guard behind PERF.181: even if something else starts workers in a burst, the host cannot be filled.

## [8.0.2216] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A burst of map requests can no longer start over a hundred queue workers and run the server out of memory.

### Fixed
- **PERF.181: the server ran out of memory and the kernel killed MySQL during a New galaxy run.** Every Galaxy Map request that queues a tile asked the worker starter for upkeep workers, and requests arriving together each counted "none starting" before any of them recorded its own start, so each launched the whole set. On 2026-10-24 about 130 workers of 125 MB took all 16 GB of a host with no swap. Only one caller at a time now counts and starts the workers of a queue, and a started worker counts as starting for 90 seconds (it was 15) so a host that is slow to load a worker is not given a second one for the same need.

### Added
- **`scripts/enable-swap.sh`** makes a swap file (8 GB by default), switches it on and adds it to `/etc/fstab` so it stays on after a reboot; it does nothing when swap is already on. `install.sh` and `update.sh` warn when the host has no swap, and INSTALL.md has a Swap section and a requirements row.

## [8.0.2215] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The Queue page lists the runs in Redis with their stages and time left, cancel stops a run at once, and a stuck run can be cleared.

### Changed
- **The Queue page shows runs, not job trees (PERF.99).** `/admin/queue` lists the runs in Redis newest first, each with its stage, how far it is, the time left and whether it has stopped answering. `/admin/queue/<run id>` shows one run's stages and the tail of its log, with cancel, clear and delete. The old job tree pages and the lease clear are gone; API version 6 (`/api/admin/work` returns runs, `/log` is new).
- **Cancel is instant (PERF.99).** Cancelling a run takes its waiting units off the queue and sends the stop command to the started ones in one pass (0.1 s for 4,000 units), and the machine is free at once. A run that has stopped answering, or whose follower process is gone, can be cleared from the page.
- **Run logs are kept (PERF.99).** Each run's event stream is written to `runs/<run id>.log` in the jobs directory when it ends, the last 20 kept, with a download link on the run's page.
- **The Generate page lists a job's runs (PERF.99).** The job page has a Runs panel linking each run and its log, and Cancel job cancels the job's live runs at once instead of waiting for the step to notice.

## [8.0.2214] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The chance that a planet is a water world now rises with its mass as in the Bern population synthesis.

### Changed
- **Row b4 (GEN.510).** The water-rich share depends on mass through the logistic fitted to the Bern synthesis (6.1 Earth masses is the centre), with a flagged plateau bracket of 0 to 1; it was a snow-line weight with no mass dependence. The comparison with the observed densities of M-dwarf planets is still open. The recipes are not read by the generator yet, so no generated value changes.

## [8.0.2213] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The envelope rows of the atmosphere recipes are tuned to the observed radius valley.

### Added
- **Rows e1 and e2 are tuned to the Kepler radius valley (GEN.509).** A simulated Kepler survey (`physics/radius_valley.py`) reproduces the published valley slope (-0.11) and its radius at 10 days (1.84 Earth radii) along one degenerate ridge of the starting envelope and the loss efficiency; the rows draw on that ridge. Two new tuning targets. The recipes are not read by the generator yet, so no generated value changes.

## [8.0.2212] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The database layer and the edit pages convert AU, km, years and parsecs through the one unit registry, with the same numbers.

### Changed
- `db/store.py` (the 67 AU-to-km and km-to-AU conversions of star, pair, comet and binary rows, the orbit clock and the SQL year constants), `db/query.py`, `db/edits.py`, `db/precision.py`, `db/orbit_trees.py`, `db/point_columns.py`, `db/sector_paths.py`, `db/column_units.py` and `admin/edits.py` call `unit_registry.converter` instead of a typed factor (GEN.571, fourth file group). Every replaced expression gives the same float bit for bit, so the stored values and the SQL text are unchanged. `db/objectindex.KM_PER_LY` is left for the epoch-changing pass: the registry's light-year-to-km factor differs from it in the last digit.

## [8.0.2211] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The tide that heats an icy moon now feeds the ocean's life under its ice, so Europa- and Enceladus-like moons score on their real heat.

### Changed
- **Tides in the chemical energy of an ice-covered ocean.** `hydrosphere.generate_hydrosphere` kept the tide of an icy moon only long enough to thicken or thin its ice lid and then threw it away; the chemical energy term of the habitability score read the radiogenic heat alone, one to three orders of magnitude too low for a Europa or an Enceladus. The tide (`tidal_flux_w_m2`) is now kept on the moon, and `habitability_world.generate` adds it to the moon's own heat flow before the energy term (1 percent of the heat flow, as for any body).
- **Migration 0152, schema v152.** `planets` and `moons` gain `tidal_flux_w_m2` (DOUBLE, nullable; a planet keeps NULL). The forced eccentricity behind a tide is not stored, so a moon saved earlier keeps NULL and its energy flux; only a moon generated now has it. Generator epoch bumped.
- **A moved planet's moons are scored again (GEN.704).** `validation.reconcile_moved_planet` refreshed a moon's air for its parent's new distance from the star but kept the dose, UV and habitability it had drawn at the old one; each moon that keeps its class now gets `generate_spin`, which ends with them, as a moved planet does.
- **The property sheet shows the tide.** `describe/sheet.py` lists `tidal_flux_w_m2` in the Water group of a planet and a moon.

## [8.0.2200] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A planet's or moon's ocean and ice are now as deep as compressed water really is: a world with a tenth of its mass in water has a 746 km layer, not the 1,047 km of a fixed density.

### Changed
- **The compressed water layer (GEN.461).** `planetgen.physics.water_layer` integrates the water over the covered area from the surface down: the density of water rises with the pressure through the liquid, ice VI, ice VII and ice X (the materials table's 300 K points), and the gravity at depth follows the mass below it. It matches the integrated reference of the design (part C 2.4) within 1 percent from a ten-thousandth to half of the mass. The liquid ends at the liquidus of the bottom temperature (the melting curves of ice III, V and VI, recomputed from the Journaux splines); under it the water is high-pressure ice and the ocean is sealed from the rock.
- **Real kilometres.** `ocean_depth_km`, `ice_shell_km` and `hp_ice_km` are the compressed thicknesses now, not water-equivalent ones. At Earth gravity the deepest liquid is 65 km at 280 K and 88 km at 300 K (it was 73 and 111), and a column is sealed from about 5e-3 of the mass. Rogue planets read the same module.
- **Stored (schema 151).** `planets` and `moons` gain `water_base_pressure_pa`, the pressure under the water (NULL for a gas giant, a dry body and a row made before this release).
- The old `max_liquid_depth_km`, `split_column` and their fixed densities (1050 and 1300 kg/m3) are gone.
- Generator epoch bump (numbered at merge): the ocean depth, the lid, the high-pressure ice and the ocean class of every watery planet and moon change, and with the ocean class the pH and water-activity draws that follow.

**Headline:** A comet's organic material now has one density, the shared table's, so a comet nucleus is a little lighter than before.

The 2 g/cm3 was attributed to Choukroun et al. 2020 in the design note without the paper having been read, so it is gone. ## [8.0.2196] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The greenhouse optical depth of an atmosphere is now worked out from its gases as a spectrum, and a bug that made very thick atmospheres far too hot in the greenhouse closure is fixed; nothing a visitor sees changes yet.

### Changed
- **GEN.703: the infrared optical depth (tau0) of an air comes from its mixture.** A new module (`physics/infrared_opacity.py`) builds the depth on a wavenumber grid from each gas's bands, their far wings, the water vapour continuum and the collision-induced pairs, as the equivalent grey thickness at the surface temperature, instead of one fixed strength per gas. A trace gas on a cold world now counts through its saturated bands, a band far from the surface's Planck peak counts for nothing, and the opacity follows the temperature. `atmosphere_state.greenhouse_warming` uses it (the per-gas strengths are gone). Earth's air gives `G` 0.65 (measured 0.625), a Venus-like air 76 (99.6), a Mars-like air 0.075 (0.10 to 0.21). The band and wing strengths are labelled stand-ins until real line data are in. It is not on the generation path yet, so no generated value moves.
- **The greenhouse closure no longer overheats very thick atmospheres.** Above an optical depth of about 500 the integral of `greenhouse.surface_temperature_k` stepped over the part that counts and returned temperatures several times too high; it now matches the published table from 1 to 200,000, and is a few times faster.

## [8.0.2192] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Every scored planet and moon carries four life scores, Microbial, Flora, Fauna and Sentient, each 0 (none) to 9 (abundant), in place of the old habitability numbers.

### Changed
- **Four life scores (GEN.649).** `planetgen/physics/life_scores.py` rates the life on a world from the evolutionary path its timeline reached and its surface conditions: Microbial from abiogenesis on, Flora from photosynthesis (at most 3 until multicellular life), Fauna from multicellularity (never more than Flora), Sentient from a technological civilization (in proportion to its first 10 Myr). A body with a life chemistry always has a timeline now (see below). The system page prints them as whole numbers where it printed "Microbial 0.00 . Complex life 0.00 . Human operability 0.52".
- **The old scores are gone.** `phi_bio`, `phi_cpx` and `phi_tech` are no longer stored or served; the human operability number (`Phi_tech`) and its four factors are removed from `planetgen/physics/habitability.py`. The two life likelihoods stay in memory for the life draw (`life.life_ceiling`).
- **Migration 0150, schema v150.** `planets` and `moons` gain `life_microbial`, `life_flora`, `life_fauna` and `life_sentient`; a galaxy made earlier gets them from the two likelihoods and the evolutionary path its rows stored, and the three old columns are dropped. The migration draws nothing; the generator epoch is for the two changes below.
- **Every planet and moon with a life chemistry has an evolutionary path (Boss, 2026-10-23; GEN.649).** A moon or a cold-zone world that the class and the habitability index allow life on gets a timeline like a planet in the ecosphere, so it can reach Flora, Fauna and Sentient. (Species and civilizations are still stored for planets only.)
- **Food is made from Flora and Fauna (Boss, 2026-10-23; GEN.653).** The Suitability food rung reads the scores: Flora is always good food (Green), Flora with Fauna is better (Blue), Fauna counts as food on its own, microbes alone are Yellow, no life Red. This moves Suitability, and so the overall score, of every world with life.

## [8.0.2185] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A world's drawn dust haze now decides whether a visitor should wear a dust filter.

### Changed
- **Airborne dust feeds the dust filter (GEN.658).** The stored dust optical depth (`tau_dust`) and the air's scale height give the dust in the air at the ground (`aerosols.dust_loading_mg_m3`, in mg/m3). From 0.1 mg/m3 (the NASA limit for Mars dust over 30 days) a dust filter is recommended, and from 10 mg/m3 it is required; a world with air and a dusty dry surface now lists it, and a sealed suit reads it as dust-tight seals. A body under 10 kPa still needs the filter or seals as before. The toxicity half waits for the surface composition to be stored. Derived from stored values, so there is no epoch or migration; `planetgen rescore-habitability` updates old galaxies.

## [8.0.2180] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A giant planet's radius, heavy elements and layered interior are now drawn together, from the star's own light and age.

### Changed
- **Giant planet radius** (GEN.460): a gas giant's radius now comes from the Fortney, Marley and Barnes 2007 tables for its mass, its heavy-element core, the light it gets from its star and its age, plus the Sestovic, Demory and Queloz 2018 swelling of close-in giants. Ice giants, gas dwarfs, giants under 17 Earth masses and bodies too rich in heavy elements for the tables keep the earlier mass-radius relation, kept inside their class's radius range.
- **Giant planet heavy elements and layers** (GEN.642): a class J giant's mass of heavy elements follows Chachan et al. 2025 with its scatter; ice giants and gas dwarfs draw a share of their mass. The interior is then drawn layer by layer (molecular and metallic envelope, helium rain, dilute and compact core, ice mantle) and its totals are the giant's bulk composition, replacing the stand-in envelope and core shares. Ices appear only beyond the star's snow line.
- The physical plausibility check bounds a giant's gravity by its class's mass and radius ranges, since no single radius law fits all the ways a giant's radius is now found.
- Generator epoch 80: every giant's radius, density and composition are new draws, and the planet draws after them move.

## [8.0.2177] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Asteroid belts, comets and interstellar comets are now made of real materials, and their densities and masses follow from what they are made of.

### Changed
- **A belt's makeup is drawn from the asteroid types of its place around its star (GEN.442).** The belt reads its star's stored snow line: dry and igneous types inside, hydrated carbonaceous types in the middle, ice-rich types beyond it. Each type is a mix of rows of the shared materials table with a porosity, and the belt's text names the largest parts with the four-level words. The kernel is a flagged stand-in until GEN.473.
- **A comet nucleus is a mix of ices, silicate dust and organics with a porosity, and its mass follows (GEN.442).** The refractory-to-ice ratio, the organic share, the porosity and the volatile percentages of water come from the comet population; the old fixed density of 533 kg/m3 is gone.
- **A standalone asteroid field is a mixture of the asteroid taxa of its family (GEN.477, field half).** The eight families are a gated table with the old frequencies marked as stand-ins; a collisional field is one taxon, dust has no pores, and the class reference page names the taxa each family is made of. The list of 84 names stays as a vocabulary only.
- **Small icy bodies and rings have their makeup and compaction draws (GEN.442).** A Kuiper belt object, dwarf planet or class D body draws a rock fraction around 0.70 and takes the tapered brittle porosity law of Bierson and Nimmo (porosity closed between 1e19 and 1e21 kg); a ring's ice fraction rises past the disk's ice line. These are ready for the bodies that will call them.

## [8.0.2175] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Every star now draws its birth [Fe/H] first, and its lifetime, subgiant and giant branch and horizontal-branch colour follow that composition.

### Changed

- **A star's composition comes before the star (GEN.651).** `birth_fe_h` draws a star's [Fe/H] from its population at its place (or its cluster's or satellite's own distribution) ahead of every other draw. The main-sequence lifetime (Hurley, Pols and Tout 2000), the end of the subgiant phase, the red giant branch and its tip, the Wolf-Rayet threshold and the horizontal-branch colour all read it, so a metal-poor star lives and brightens differently from a metal-rich one of the same mass. `star_params` carries it as `metallicity_fe_h`.
- **The bright-star sampler keeps one table per composition.** The cell bounds of a sampling table hold only for the composition they were built at, so `star_population` builds a table for each 0.25 dex bin of [Fe/H] (`tuning.BRIGHT_TABLE_FE_H_STEP_DEX`), takes each cell's bound over the bin's two edges and its centre with the stretch of every phase window (`tuning.BRIGHT_TABLE_BOUND_MARGIN`), and draws a star's composition in proportion to the stars each composition can make (`_draw_fe_h`), so a metal-poor place no longer fills its bright giants with stars its composition cannot make. The workers warm every bin.
- **Stand-ins until GEN.661 and GEN.662.** The expected count of bright stars still uses the share at the reference composition, and a cluster or satellite star is drawn at the reference composition rather than its component's value. The lifetime fit's metallicity is held to the range the Hurley, Pols and Tout formulae were fitted over (Z 0.0001 to 0.03), so a very metal-poor star no longer extrapolates.

## [8.0.2167] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The Galaxy Map's data can now be read as sector-block nodes, with the light of every block stored, the first step to one continuous map that has no zoom stages.

### Added
- **Sector-block nodes (MAP.260).** `GET /api/galaxy/nodes` and the site's `/galaxy/nodes` answer by block of the ladder (a sector, or a block of 3 to 177,147 shells): the brightest stars, generated stars, point phenomena and clouds inside the block, the sums of what is stored about it (its generated sectors and the light of the stars and phenomena scattered in it), and for a level-3 block or a sector the sectors placed in it. A block lists every object of its parent that lies inside it. The site caches each node on disk beside the tiles; a change to a sector drops the nodes of its chain, and the browser is told which, as it is for tiles.

A scatter, a clear and the map-luminosity fill make it at their end; the migration fills it from the stored scatter, which can take a while on a big galaxy.
- **The block totals follow a `galaxy` run.** A run now brings the sectors it saved into `galaxy_block_stats` and `galaxy_block_lights` once at its end. **Headline:** The frozen nitrogen air of a rogue planet and the boiling point of water now come from the one vapour-pressure function.

## [8.0.2165] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The bright-star backfill draws the stars of a sparse block of cells with one count for the block instead of a draw in every cell.

### Changed
- **The backfill picks its draw path per block (GEN.309).** A block (a band's 256 cells) whose largest per-cell rate in a luminosity or mass band is under 0.05 stars now draws that band's stars block first: one Poisson count for the block, each candidate kept with the chance its cell's own rate asks, and each kept star on a stream of its own (`bright_stars.block_candidates`, built in GEN.308). Denser blocks draw cell by cell as before. The choice depends on the block and the band alone, so a sector gets the same stars whichever other sectors a run reaches, in whatever order, split between workers or restricted to a region. The stars a seed gives in the sparse blocks (the outer disk, the halo, the far edge) are different draws of the same distribution, so existing galaxies keep what they hold and new ones differ there.

## [8.0.2162] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** White dwarfs now have the binary kinds astronomers see: close double white dwarfs, post-common-envelope pairs, cataclysmic variables, AM Canum Venaticorum binaries, and barium and symbiotic giants.

### Added
- **Close double white dwarfs and post-common-envelope pairs.** 9.5% of white dwarfs have a white dwarf companion within 4 AU that has not merged by the system's age, and about 3% of white dwarfs a post-common-envelope companion within 2 AU, some of them hot subdwarfs.
- **Cataclysmic variables and AM CVn binaries.** 6.5 in 10,000 white dwarfs accrete from a lobe-filling star at a period of 1.3 to 10 hours (36% with a magnetic white dwarf), and 7.5 in 100,000 from a helium star at 5 to 65 minutes. Only these two draws make a white dwarf pair `accreting`.
- **White dwarf merger products.** 10% of old white dwarfs are flagged as merger products with a rejuvenated age.
- **Barium and symbiotic giants.** 1% of G and K giants are barium or CH stars and 5 in a million are symbiotic, each with a white dwarf companion on the observed orbits (new member flags `barium`, `symbiotic` and `magnetic`).

### Changed
- **Generated systems change.** The white dwarf companion odds, the new draws and the white dwarf pair rules move the draws of star systems, so every galaxy regenerates differently (generator epoch recorded).

## [8.0.2161] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Debug mode now writes every decision of a run, the queue workers' included, to stdout and to the debug log.

### Changed
- **Debug mode writes everything to stdout, and every command takes it (Boss).** `planetgen system --debug` printed 3 lines because the generator runs in a queue worker whose stdout goes nowhere; the decisions, draws and SQL of every unit reached only the debug log file. A debug run (`--debug`, or `"debug": true` in `config.json`) now relays the lines of its workers through Redis to the command that started the run, which prints them as they are written, in one ISO-timestamp line format shared with the debug log. A command whose result goes to stdout (`--output -`) writes its debug lines to stderr.
- **More of what a run decides is logged.** Draws on a `draw.Stream` a generator holds (the scatters, the sampling helpers), bulk draws, gamma and Dirichlet draws and new streams with their seeds; the run's stages, units, worker starts and the machine's lease; SQL transactions and pooled connections; page, tile and component-field cache hits and misses; the worker's own start, restart and exit.
- **Every command takes `--debug` and `--debug-areas`.** All 24 `planetgen` subcommands already did; so do now the 18 `python3 -m planetgen.cli.*` commands and the worker, and the Generate page has a Debug box that adds `--debug` to every step of a job, so the job log shows the decisions.
- **`--debug-areas`, `"debug_areas"` and `PLANETGEN_DEBUG_AREAS` limit the output.** Areas: `decision`, `draw`, `sql`, `queue`, `cache`, `web`, `lib`; a leading `-` leaves one out. Empty, the default, writes everything but `branch`. Errors and normal output always show.
- **A new `branch` area logs every conditional jump in our own code (Boss), off unless named.** `--debug-areas branch` (or `all,branch`) writes, for each `if`, loop test and conditional expression the program runs, its source line, whether the jump was taken, the line it went to and the values the line refers to; the decisions that are neither random nor narrated. It uses `sys.monitoring`, writes about 750,000 lines for one system and runs about 15 times slower.

Every replaced expression gives the same float bit for bit, pinned by `tests/test_unit_converters.py`. The module-level `KM_PER_PC` of `galaxy/straight_line` and `galaxy/frame` and the one of `galaxy/ejecta_field` are gone; nothing else read them.

## [8.0.2159] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The research behind the moons of ejected and isolated planets is written down with its sources and its gaps.

### Added
- `docs/design/systems/wanderer-moon-sources.md` (GEN.560, the remaining parts): the share of moons that stay bound when their planet is ejected (Debes and Sigurdsson 2007, Rabago and Steffen 2018, Huang and Lai 2026: about 0.7 to 0.85 inside 0.01 Hill radii, 0.48 at 0.1) and the disks of isolated planetary-mass objects (disk fraction 42 to 46 percent, dust mass 0.07 to 0.63 Earth masses at 12 Jupiter masses). The recalled "Hong et al. 2018" is not a paper that has the numbers and is replaced; the disk size limit stays a stand-in. No behaviour change.

## [8.0.2158] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A generation stage whose longest unit ran over five minutes is now reported in the run's log.

### Changed
- **A unit-length ceiling (PERF.155).** New setting `queue.unit_ceiling_seconds` (default 300, "Unit length ceiling" under Speed and disk): the longest one unit of a generation stage is meant to run. When a stage ends and its longest unit ran longer, the run's log says so, naming the stage and how many units it was cut into.
- Every queued command now says whether its stage is one unit by nature or how long its longest unit runs at the default galaxy size, and a test fails for a new command that says neither, or says more than the ceiling.

## [8.0.2157] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Survival equipment now sits under the habitability rows that ask for it, not under a Blue one.

### Fixed
- **Equipment items in the wrong rows (GEN.702).** An item names every PHI-6 category it can come from and is listed under those that are not Blue: a cold world's self-contained air is under Temperature, not under a Blue Air row; a hardened pressure suit is under Pressure and Radiation; and a suit that seals (pressure, armoured) is also listed under Temperature and Air where those ask for gear. The API's equipment items gain `domains`.

## [8.0.2156] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A system asked to have both an asteroid belt and a habitable world no longer loses the belt on a small red dwarf now and then.

### Fixed
- **A forced asteroid belt or habitable world could be trimmed away after the planet attempts had kept it (TEST.313).** The star's age settles after the attempts and only rises; the survival limit falls with age, so the last trim sometimes took the belt of an M5V star (about 2 systems in 300). The planet attempts now run once more under the settled age before the request is given up as unmet.

## [8.0.2155] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A world is now called habitable when its overall PHI-6 colour is Blue or Green, in one place, instead of by its class letter.

### Changed
- **One definition of habitable (GEN.643).** `habitability.is_habitable(phi4)` is true for an overall Blue or Green score. The API's `habitable` flag, the Habitable and Habitable moon chips on the system page, the per-system `hab_count` and the description's count all use it. The old class test is served as `habitable_class` (the "Habitable class" chip stays).
- **The request for a habitable world still steers by the class list.** The generator draws the class before the score, so `+habitable_world` guarantees a world of a life class (`StarSystem.habitable_class_count`), which may score below Green. The sector directive `habitable>=N` counts the same. This changes when the classes are derived from conditions.
- No stored value or draw changes, so there is no generator epoch and no migration.
- **The fallback for a request that falls short (Boss, 2026-10-23).** `habitability.habitable_request_result(overall, suitability)` says `"aim"` for a Blue or Green world and `"fallback"` for an overall Yellow whose Suitability (the sustainability factor) is at least Yellow. `StarSystem.habitable_request` (also set on a loaded system) is `"aim"`, `"fallback"` or `"unmet"` for a system generated with a habitable world requested, `None` otherwise. The generation retry does not steer on it yet (that needs a regenerate under restricted draws), so `"unmet"` still happens.

## [8.0.2154] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The stars of a system are drawn as a tree, so systems of three or more stars now come out of the fill.

### Changed
- **A system draws its stars from the `star-count` table (GEN.631).** The one-companion draw and its per-class chances are gone: the primary's stars and the orbits between them are one tree (`draw_member_tree`), with the number of stars the table gives for its class (most O and B stars are not alone, and a G star has three or more stars in about a tenth of systems). The two stars of the tree's pair are the primary and secondary as before, and each further star is a member of the system, stored and shown with its place in the tree; members have no planets of their own yet. A brown dwarf, a neutron star or a black hole among a living star's companions is left out, since none can be built as a star of a pair. The widest orbit is still the place's, and `+binary_system`, `+wide_binary` and the binary prevalences ask for the same things. The system's seed gives different stars than before.
- **A stored tree of three or more stars is built.** A scattered star whose members are all ordinary stars is built with all of them, not the first alone, and its stored rows are spent.
- **The pair's kind follows its axis.** A pair is a `close` (circumbinary) pair under 0.25 AU and a `wide` pair otherwise, whatever the tree called the orbit; its node carries that kind.
- **The shares of binaries and wide pairs the Generate page starts from** are remeasured: 23.9% of systems have a pair and 81.0% of the pairs are wide.

- **The star count settings reach the draw (GEN.267).** `--stars N` forces the number of stars (a count the tree cannot give a star, such as a pair around a star at the hydrogen-burning limit, is reported as unmet), `--max-stars` caps the tree, and the `multi_star` prevalence scales the chance of five or more.

### Removed
- **The metallicity factor on close companions** (GEN.103) no longer reaches the fill, and its audit (TEST.196) is removed with the draw it checked; the tree does not take the factor yet.

The 177,147 root is one row cut into three wedges and holds the whole grid. ## [8.0.2152] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Every star now carries its own ultraviolet-C share, and a planet or moon's ground light and UV index can be read from what it stores.

### Added
- **GEN.443: the ground light of a stored body.** `physics/body_radiation.py` turns a planet's or moon's record (its air, its star and distance, its ozone column and its haze, dust and cloud) into the band spectrum at its ground with the two-stream model, and gives its UV index and DNA dose. Migration 0145 adds `stars.uv_c_share` (schema v145), the share of the star's blackbody UV-C it gives off, drawn once from the star's own stream (log-uniform 0.1 to 1); a row saved before it keeps NULL and reads as the blackbody until the galaxy is regenerated.

## [8.0.2151] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A body's radius, density and gravity can be worked out from its mass and bulk composition: a reference solver and the fast fits for dry rock, water worlds and sub-Neptunes.

### Added
- **Bulk structure kernels (GEN.429).** `planetgen.physics.bulk_structure` gives `structure(bulk, mass_kg)`: the radius at the 1 bar level, mean density, surface gravity and escape speed of a body from its `BulkFractions`. The reference solver `layered_structure` integrates an iron core, a silicate mantle and a water layer (liquid water from IAPWS-95, the ice VI, VII and X points of the materials table and the Seager polytrope above 1 TPa) and reproduces part B's check numbers (Earth-sized planet 0.9996 Earth radii, moment of inertia 0.331) and part C's water-world radii within 1 percent. The fast forms are part B's fit for dry rock (0.1 to 20 Earth masses), part C's closed form for water-bearing bodies (0.3 to 20) and Lopez and Fortney's core and envelope laws (1 to 20); outside them the solver runs, below 1e21 kg the zero-pressure mixing rule gives a heap of grains, and a giant is refused (GEN.460). Inverses give the core fraction or water fraction from a mass and radius (route 1).
- Pure functions with no draws: nothing is generated or stored differently, so no generator epoch. `DATA-LICENSE.md` records the NIST WebBook water isotherm.

## [8.0.2150] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Every planet and moon now has a bulk composition (iron, rock, water, other ices, envelope) drawn from its star's own abundances, and its mass, density and gravity follow from it.

### Changed
- **The composition comes first (GEN.428, GEN.429).** `planetgen.physics.bulk_draw` takes the host star's own number ratios (Fe, Si, Al, Ca and Ni against Mg, and C/O, from `stellar_abundances` for the star's abundance key) and builds the rock (MgO, SiO2, CaO, Al2O3 and FeO) and the iron core (the Fe the mantle does not hold, Ni, and light elements) from them: a Sun-like star gives a core mass fraction near 0.3 and an iron-rich star a bigger one. The class still sets the radius; the mass is the one that radius holds for that composition (`bulk_structure.structure`, found by bisection), so density and gravity are results and no longer a draw from the class's density range. A body given a mass keeps it and its radius follows; a body given both, and class S, work the core fraction back from them (`composition_origin` is `inverse`).
- **What is drawn** is only what the star cannot say: the kind of rock (silicate, or silicon carbide and graphite for a star of C/O 0.8 or more and for class C, through the new gated table `bulk-rock-kind`), the water share (the same class ranges as before, now drawn with the composition and read by the hydrosphere), the other ices of an icy class (from the comet volatile proportions), the mantle's FeO, the core's light elements, a small body's porosity and a carbon body's graphite. Giants get a stand-in envelope and heavy-element core until the giant interiors (GEN.460).
- **Stored (DB.69, schema 144).** `planets` and `moons` gain `metal_mass_fraction`, `rock_mass_fraction`, `ice_mass_fraction`, `envelope_mass_fraction` (with `water_mass_fraction` they add up to 1), `rock_feo_fraction`, `rock_al2o3_fraction`, `rock_mg_si_ratio`, `envelope_helium_fraction`, `envelope_z_fraction`, `porosity`, `carbon_rock` and `composition_origin`. Rows saved before the migration keep them empty; `bulk_composition.bulk_fractions(body)` returns `None` for them.
- The unused `calculate_object_mass` is gone; `hydrosphere.generate_hydrosphere` no longer draws the water share (it reads the body's).
- Generator epoch 70: every planet's and moon's mass, density, gravity and water share are new draws, the planet draws that follow them move, and the radiogenic heat reads the body's own rock share and Al2O3.

## [8.0.2146] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** A planet page now states one pace, one chemistry and one set of milestones and ages for its life, so its paragraphs can no longer contradict each other.

### Fixed
- **GEN.666: the life paragraphs disagreed.** A page could say "life based on melanin would evolve at a normal pace" and, a paragraph later, "life here would evolve at a hyper-accelerated pace ... technological civilization, reached at 80 Myr". The pace was drawn twice (`life.get_evolutionary_speed` and a second draw inside `evolution.get_evolutionary_state`), stored in two columns and written by two writers. The generator now draws the pace once (`evolution.draw_scale`, one the star supports and the life chemistry needs) and stores it in `evolutionary_pace` for every body with a life chemistry. `evolutionary_speed` is dropped (migration 0143, schema v143; a body that had only a speed keeps it as its pace). `describe/life_facts.py` resolves the chemistry, pace, ages and milestone once into a `LifeFacts` and the life paragraph and the timeline paragraph are written from it alone; the timeline no longer repeats a pace of its own and says when the system was that old at the milestone. The unused second writer (`Planet._generate_life_and_flavor_paragraphs`, `evolution.timeline_paragraphs`) is removed.
- **A world whose life does not split water is no longer told it releases oxygen.** The "photosynthesis" milestone is named and described by the chemistry's metabolism (`tuning.LIFE_METABOLISMS`): oxygenic photosynthesis, anoxygenic photosynthesis, retinal phototrophy or radiotrophy.
- A body with no viable life chemistry no longer keeps a reflection spectrum.
- **The atmosphere table now holds the class's balance gases.** A class B page said "a mix of helium, sodium, and oxygen" above a table of "Oxygen 100%": helium and sodium (the class's balance, named in the phrase and held in the surface pressure) were left out of the table. The table is now shares of the whole surface pressure (`physics/atmosphere.balance_names` and `balance_kpa`).

## [8.0.2144] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** The text description of a body now keeps each quantity in the unit it is stored in, and converts it only when it is shown.

### Changed
- **Describe quantities** (GEN.574): a quantity in the description model is `{"kind", "value", "unit"}` instead of `{"kind", "si"}`. `model.qty` checks the unit against the unit registry and `model.measured` keeps the stored quantity's own unit, so a length held in megametres is no longer converted to metres on the way in. The wiki, text and web renderers convert to the kind's base unit when they show it; the page's `data-si` attribute, which the browser reads, is unchanged. What you see on a body page does not change.

## [8.0.2143] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Twelve physics files now convert astronomical units, years, light-years and parsecs through the one unit registry, with the same numbers.

### Changed
- `unit_registry.converter(from_key, to_key)` returns a function for one conversion, looked up once when a module loads: a multiply by the larger-to-smaller ratio or a divide by the smaller-to-larger one, a power of ten taken as the exact power, so it gives the same float as the hand-written `* 1000.0`, `/ AU_TO_KM` or `* SECONDS_PER_YEAR` it replaces.
- Twelve files (`activity`, `body_positions`, `body_state`, `formation`, `hosting_gate`, `kepler`, `orbits`, `planet_survival`, `planet_zones`, `pre_main_sequence`, `stability`, `system_tree`) use it for their AU, km, m, light-year, parsec, year, second and Gyr conversions (GEN.571, first file group). `tests/test_unit_converters.py` holds each conversion against the expression it replaced on 7,000 inputs, bit for bit. The module-level `AU_KM` of `body_positions` and `system_tree`, `SECONDS_PER_YEAR` of `system_tree` and `YEAR_S` of `pre_main_sequence` are gone; nothing else read them.

## [8.0.2135] - 2026-10-24

**Headline:** Close binaries now come in their observed kinds: contact binaries, Algols, blue stragglers, merger products, Be stars with a stripped companion, and the rare R Coronae Borealis, FK Comae and Thorne-Zytkow stars.

### Added
- **Contact binaries and Algols follow their gates.** A contact binary of a solar-type primary needs an age of at least 0.1 Gy, an Algol an age under 3 Gy, and neither holds a contracting or substellar object. The donor of an Algol that was the heavier at birth carries `mass_reversed`, and the lighter star is a `mass_gainer`. The tight tail of the period law is calibrated (`tight_tail_weight` 6.0): about 0.5% of FGK systems hold a contact binary, and 60% of contact binaries have a tertiary.
- **Merger products and mass gainers.** 8% of young massive stars are merger products with one star fewer and a rejuvenated age, 0.5% of older stars are blue stragglers, and 20% of young massive stars are mass gainers.
- **Be stars.** 20% of young B stars are Be stars, and 30% of those have a stripped helium companion that spun them up.
- **R Coronae Borealis, FK Comae and Thorne-Zytkow stars.** Old giants take these at the catalogue's Galaxy counts; a Thorne-Zytkow object is a single member flagged theoretical.
- **Eclipsing and spectroscopic pairs** are derived from a tree (`MemberTree.eclipsing_nodes`, `spectroscopic_nodes`), not stored.

### Changed
- **Generated systems change.** The period law, the gates and the new draws move the draws of star systems, so every galaxy regenerates differently (generator epoch recorded).

**Headline:** The retired `/<name>.py` page addresses and the old NAV parameter style now answer 404 instead of redirecting.

### Removed
- The `/<name>.py` redirects (`index.py`, `search.py`, `sector.py` and the rest) and `web/old_urls.py`; those addresses now give the normal 404 page.
- The old NAV parameters (`from_id`, `to_id`, `from_kind`, `to_kind`, `from_type`, `to_type`), which used to redirect to the current `from`/`to` form.
